texture/16roof.bmp@efd76845.description: Wooden shingles in three staggered rows, each a different shade of brown and tan, black gaps and weathered edges.
texture/16roof.bmp@efd76845.usage: Qeynos and Tutorial roofs at about 14 units per repeat. Cheap shingle roof for sheds and houses at 12 to 16 units; warm and varied. Classic-era image, a little soft and dark; the shingle size is large, so keep rows horizontal.

texture/ab_fp_ext_stucco_red_c.dds@7a469.description: Dusty warm-brown stucco speckled with pale pits and chipped-off patches; a dry sun-worn adobe look.
texture/ab_fp_ext_stucco_red_c.dds@7a469.usage: Freeport Arena exterior walls at about 12 units per repeat. Adobe house walls and boundary walls at 10 to 14 units, darker and earthier than the peach kurn plaster. Despite the red in its name it reads brown; mix it with terracotta trim.

texture/ab_fstent_leather01_c.dds@7cb85c.description: Pale tan hide-canvas with fine wrinkles and soft darker streaks; even, bright and calm.
texture/ab_fstent_leather01_c.dds@7cb85c.usage: Arcstone tent walls and roofs (overhanging, models only) at about 26 units per repeat. Light shade cloth and awning at 12 to 24 units; blends with sandstone and plaster. Its normal map is ab_fstent_leather01_n_5.

texture/av_canvas01_c.dds@cc89fd1e.description: Khaki canvas drawn taut with soft folds radiating from the middle to each corner, as if stretched on a frame; fine woven grain.
texture/av_canvas01_c.dds@cc89fd1e.usage: Tent roofs of Dranik's Hollows and Proving Grounds, on overhanging and sloped surfaces, about 37 units per repeat on whole tent pieces. One repeat per cloth panel: awnings, tent canopies and market covers at 10 to 20 units. Not seamless; do not tile.

texture/av_rock05_c.dds@da173111.description: Dark grey-brown mottled rock with rusty stains.
texture/av_rock05_c.dds@da173111.usage: Wall of Slaughter's rock models at about 34 units per repeat with av_rock05_n: weathered boulders and outcrops, not warm canyon walls.

texture/av_rock05_n.dds@b0d60d3a.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is av_rock05_c.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/bhdrokdirt.bmp@d880c4cf.description: A one-way border: dark brown earth with grassy tufts across the top grading down through a ragged edge into broken grey-green rock.
texture/bhdrokdirt.bmp@d880c4cf.usage: Feerrott cliff bases, almost all on vertical faces, at about 100 units per repeat. Measured as not seamless: use it as a strip at a cliff or bank foot with paintTransition, dirt side toward the ground; at 20 to 30 units tall. The rock is cold and grey, so it suits grey-cave or river-cut rock rather than red cliffs.

texture/blend_sand_rock.dds@304ec155.description: Ochre rock with a thin fringe of pale sand along its lower edge; repeats across.
texture/blend_sand_rock.dds@304ec155.usage: Like blend_sand_rock_lg with a narrower sand fringe, for a rock base meeting sand on gentler ground; not placed in Sunderock's geometry. Pairs with blend_sand_rock_5n.

texture/blend_sand_rock.dds@c2f090a5.description: A one-way transition: golden-orange sun-baked rock with fibrous weathering across most of the tile, easing into a band of pale cream sand along the bottom edge.
texture/blend_sand_rock.dds@c2f090a5.usage: Commonlands blend between rock and sand. Lay with paintTransition so the bottom edge meets the sand and the top edge meets rock: cliff foot or ledge edge into plateau sand. About 24 to 32 units wide. Its normal map is blend_sand_rock_5n (a separate asset). Measured as tiling, but the pale band shows as stripes if repeated down the surface.

texture/blend_sand_rock_5n.dds@7f7b8d01.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is blend_sand_rock.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/blend_sand_rock_lg.dds@bbf9255e.description: Ochre rock over its upper two thirds fading through a ragged edge into a broad band of pale sand along the bottom; repeats across but not down.
texture/blend_sand_rock_lg.dds@bbf9255e.usage: The foot of a rock face where it meets sand: map it once vertically with the sand band at the ground line and repeat it along the wall (it tiles horizontally only); Sunderock's spires use about 20 units per repeat, and big cliffs can go to 40. Pairs with blend_sand_rock_lg10n; the rock above takes rock_light2 or rock_light5 and the ground di_tak_ruin_sand2.

texture/blend_sand_rock_lg10n.dds@de686f.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is blend_sand_rock_lg.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/bp_tent_plain01_c.dds@0eaad934.description: Warm rust-brown dyed canvas with soft darker clouds and a faint weave; plain and heavy.
texture/bp_tent_plain01_c.dds@0eaad934.usage: East Korlach tent roofs, sloped, about 21 units per repeat. Dyed awnings, tent walls and wagon covers at 12 to 22 units; a terracotta-brown cloth between the orange hide and the khaki canvas.

texture/burlap.dds@52302797.description: Coarse khaki-olive burlap with a clear crosshatch weave and slub threads.
texture/burlap.dds@52302797.usage: Used on sacks, rugs and cloths in Theatera, Ro and house archives, at about 6 units per repeat. Awning cloth, sacks and market stalls at 4 to 8 units where the weave should read. Pair with rope3 for ties.

texture/canwall1.bmp@acc2b333.description: Classic-era dark ochre canyon wall with eroded ridges and deep shadows.
texture/canwall1.bmp@acc2b333.usage: Oasis of Marr's canyon walls at about 130 units per repeat on steep slopes; softer and darker than the Underfoot rocks, for distant or shaded walls.

texture/cavedirt.dds@c36e5a17.description: Pale grey-tan crumbly dirt with fine pebble grit and small pitted shadows; a dry dusty ground.
texture/cavedirt.dds@c36e5a17.usage: Toskirakk and Cooling Chamber ground at about 52 units per repeat (flat). For canyon dry ground use 25 to 35 units. A neutral light dirt for dusty plateau, ledges and bay floors. A near-identical Loping Plains copy (@2de263e0) is a different hash.

texture/cavefloor.dds@2c7cb80e.description: Sandy tan-brown earth with fine grit and darker damp-looking blotches.
texture/cavefloor.dds@2c7cb80e.usage: Eleven client zones use this cave floor, at about 18 units per repeat on flats and gentle slopes. Bay floors, dusty yards and ordinary trodden dirt at 16 to 22 units. A reliable neutral dirt between sand and rock.

texture/cavefloordrk2_c.dds@923c5e4f.description: Plain dark brown fine earth, nearly uniform.
texture/cavefloordrk2_c.dds@923c5e4f.usage: Cave floors and shaded ground: Goru'kar Mesa's grass-dirt recipe at about 10 units per repeat.

texture/cavetrail.dds@bb50b2eb.description: Smooth dusty rose-red clay with faint lighter vertical streaks and soft pits; a pinkish-red earth with little detail, 512 pixels wide.
texture/cavetrail.dds@bb50b2eb.usage: Scarlet and The Grey used it on slopes and steep banks at about 55 units per repeat. A red clay bank, gully wall or trail at 30 to 50 units. Pink-cool compared with orange sands; plain, so lay pebbles or dirt over it. cavefloor.dds@bc1b12c3 is a near-identical sibling.

texture/cavewall.dds@568482fc.description: The same rose-red sandstone as cavewall2 with its marks running vertically: runnels and cracks top to bottom.
texture/cavewall.dds@568482fc.usage: Vertical companion to cavewall2 for cave roofs and walls where the grain should run down; the Scarlet Desert used it mostly on overhangs at about 55 units per repeat.

texture/cavewall001b.dds@197d4034.description: Smooth terracotta-orange sandstone in horizontal bands: a pale sandy cream top band over deeper orange layers with fine sandy grain and a few darker streaks.
texture/cavewall001b.dds@197d4034.usage: The Tak caves (taka to takj) put it on vertical and overhanging walls at about 41 units per repeat, over a quarter of one zone. Ideal for strata on a red canyon wall and for cave-bay walls. Measured as not seamless vertically: let one repeat span a wall section, or hide the repeat line under a ledge or a trim band; it repeats cleanly sideways.

texture/cavewall002c.dds@a5114a3a.description: Smooth terracotta-orange sandstone with fine sandy grain, faint horizontal streaks and softly paler clouds; the plainest, richest orange of the Tak cave set.
texture/cavewall002c.dds@a5114a3a.usage: Tak zones' walls, ceilings and flats at about 32 units per repeat (22 percent of one zone). Main body colour for a red canyon wall or a cave-bay ceiling at 28 to 40 units; tiles cleanly. Plain and saturated: break with cavewall001b strata bands and darker vt_strata below.

texture/cavewall002m.dds@fd66cef0.description: Terracotta sandstone laced with darker horizontal flow bands and wind-cut streaks, ending in a crumbly flaking dark-ochre row along the bottom edge.
texture/cavewall002m.dds@fd66cef0.usage: Tak ceilings (overhang only), about 53 units per repeat. Layered, weathered rock for bay ceilings, undercut ledges and the lip of overhangs at 40 to 55 units. Measured as not seamless: the flaky bottom row repeats as a line, so tile it once vertically or hide it behind a ledge.

texture/cavewall004b.dds@b927dec0.description: Layered orange sandstone with a pale dusty-pink top band, a darker streaked orange band across the middle and fine grit at the bottom; reads as an eroded cliff face.
texture/cavewall004b.dds@b927dec0.usage: Tak cave walls (vertical, steep and overhanging) at about 31 units per repeat. A banded face for canyon walls and cave mouths at 28 to 36 units; one repeat shows a full pale-to-dark sequence, so the bands step visibly. Measured as not seamless vertically: stack one per wall height or hide the edge behind a ledge.

texture/cavewall2.dds@ca260dbb.description: Dusty rose-red sandstone with horizontal ledges, pits, and crumbling bands; soft, low contrast detail.
texture/cavewall2.dds@ca260dbb.usage: Red canyon and cave walls: the Scarlet Desert covers its walls and cave roofs with it at about 78 units per repeat. Its horizontal ledges suit layered canyon strata; box-project on walls and keep the repeat large, as it goes soft up close.

texture/cb_rockblendleftb.dds@d588ecf3.description: A sideways transition: pale pink-grey fibrous rock fills most of the tile, fading over its left quarter into soft grey-olive earth.
texture/cb_rockblendleftb.dds@d588ecf3.usage: Loping Plains blend between rock and ground, tiling. Rock-to-dirt strips at the foot of a cliff or river cut, 20 to 30 units wide, earth side toward the ground (rotate the strip so the left edge meets the soil). cb_rockblendrightb is its mirror, for the opposite side. The fibre rock is pale and cool, so it suits grey or pinkish rock.

texture/cb_rockblendrightb.dds@eca72bec.description: A sideways transition: pale pink-grey fibrous rock fills most of the tile, fading over its right quarter into soft grey-olive earth; the mirror of cb_rockblendleftb.
texture/cb_rockblendrightb.dds@eca72bec.usage: Loping Plains blend between rock and ground, tiling. Use for the opposite bank of a cut or the other side of a rock band, 20 to 30 units wide. Pair with the left version so a rock strip can fade into soil on both sides.

texture/chelsith_cliff_a_c.dds@c6f03ee1.description: Pale tan sandstone with fine horizontal strata lines.
texture/chelsith_cliff_a_c.dds@c6f03ee1.usage: Painted as a strata layer beside darker rock on canyonhousing's walls (2026-10-20) it read as cream candy stripes. Use it as the whole rock, or at low contrast against rock of its own family.

texture/cliffwall.bmp@7acce806.description: Ochre-brown rock with long vertical flutes and drips like melted candle wax, golden highlights on the ridges and dark hollows between.
texture/cliffwall.bmp@7acce806.usage: Dalnir's cliffs and cave walls (overhang and vertical) at about 22 units per repeat, 512 pixels. Warm brown fluted rock for cave-bay walls and the lower, shadowed canyon face at 18 to 28 units; flutes should run vertically. A classic-era painterly image: avoid close-up inspection and large flat areas.

texture/clz_gravel_path.dds@32178b02.description: Crisp grey and white rounded gravel stones packed tightly with dark shadows, like a well-raked path.
texture/clz_gravel_path.dds@32178b02.usage: Arena and Clz zones. Footpaths, garden yards and gravel aprons at 6 to 10 units per repeat (stones 0.3 to 0.6 unit). Cold grey: it reads as limestone gravel, so use on formal village paths and not as natural canyon ground. Pair with its normal map.

texture/clz_gravel_path_n.dds@21115178.description: Normal map of rounded gravel stones for clz_gravel_path.
texture/clz_gravel_path_n.dds@21115178.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/cobble.bmp@036aa33c.description: Rubble field-stone wall: oval blue-grey and rust-brown stones laid loosely in thick pale mortar with raised joints.
texture/cobble.bmp@036aa33c.usage: Qeynos Hills/Toqrg walls. Rustic house walls, terrace walls and well rings at 12 to 16 units per repeat; stones 1.5 to 2 units wide. Mixed grey and rust colours suit a village next to sandstone. Dated, a little blurred; use at medium distance.

texture/cobblefloor01_c.dds@feb23f10.description: Large rounded flagstones of orange-brown with olive blotches, separated by soft pale-tan grout; a soft, slightly blurred look.
texture/cobblefloor01_c.dds@feb23f10.usage: Floors of Frostfang halls at about 19 units per repeat (all flat). Plaza flagstones at 12 to 16 units, stones about 3 units wide, in a warm terracotta tone. Measured as not seamless, so hide the repeat edge under borders or sand; soft focus means it reads best at distance.

texture/cobblestones.dds@a0ab496e.description: Rectangular grey-tan cobble setts in staggered rows with dark joints and pitted faces; a sharp 512-pixel image.
texture/cobblestones.dds@a0ab496e.usage: Furniture-archive cobble for small props; no measured terrain use. Town paving and low walls at 6 to 10 units per repeat (a sett about 0.6 unit). Cool grey: for a hub lane or plaza edge beside warm sand. The rows run horizontally, so lay along the road.

texture/combrick.bmp@df88a4cf.description: Dark brown-red bricks in a herringbone pattern with grey mortar and purple-brown variation.
texture/combrick.bmp@df88a4cf.usage: Paving and walls across Ro, Dreadlands and Cazic-Thule at about 13 units per repeat. Herringbone lane or courtyard paving at 10 to 14 units. Dark and slightly purple; keep for small areas near houses, not for large open ground.

texture/cracktile.bmp@a9b02d26.description: Dark red-brown curved barrel roof tiles in vertical ribs, with worn glaze, chips and pale scuffs.
texture/cracktile.bmp@a9b02d26.usage: The Hole's roof slopes at about 15 units per repeat. Mission-style roof for houses and shrines at 12 to 16 units, ribs running down the slope. Dark and maroon: reads heavier than the orange flat tiles; classic-era image with a little softness.

texture/craggy_cliff_c.dds@3ba7cac2.description: Dark brown-black craggy rock with long deep cracks, chipped plates and pale scuffs; rugged 512-pixel detail.
texture/craggy_cliff_c.dds@3ba7cac2.usage: Stone Snake cliffs at about 37 units per repeat, mostly vertical and overhanging. Dark cracked rock for the shaded foot of a canyon wall or a cave mouth at 30 to 50 units. Cold dark brown, so keep a small share beside the red-orange faces.

texture/deposits_pools.dds@dabe929d.description: Pale yellow and white mineral crust in blotchy layers, like the rim of a hot spring.
texture/deposits_pools.dds@dabe929d.usage: Rims and terraces of mineral pools on gentle slopes (Sunderock's pools recipe, slopes 8 to 23 degrees, about 13 units per repeat); bright enough to need small areas.

texture/di_atiiki_ex_sandstone.dds@fdbce.description: Grey-tan sandstone with patches of yellow-ochre and fine pitting; even grain, no joints or cracks.
texture/di_atiiki_ex_sandstone.dds@fdbce.usage: Building stone of Atiiki, Silyssar and Rathe Chamber at about 9 units per repeat, mostly on models. Good for desert ruin walls, plinths, rock-cut doorways and boulder skins at 8 to 12 units. Pair with its normal map and the sandstone steps for floors.

texture/di_atiiki_ex_sandstone_10n.dds@e.description: Fine pitted-grain normal map for di_atiiki_ex_sandstone, nearly flat.
texture/di_atiiki_ex_sandstone_10n.dds@e.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/di_atiiki_ex_sandstone_steps.dds.description: Smooth honey-tan sandstone with faint horizontal streaks of ochre; clean and even, like a cut slab.
texture/di_atiiki_ex_sandstone_steps.dds.usage: Step and floor surface of Atiiki and Silyssar at about 28 units per repeat. Good for stairs, plaza slabs and thresholds; one repeat covers several steps, so 20 to 28 units reads right. Pair with its normal map and the matching wall sandstone.

texture/di_atiiki_ex_sandstone_steps_10n.description: Soft slab-grain normal map for di_atiiki_ex_sandstone_steps.
texture/di_atiiki_ex_sandstone_steps_10n.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/di_et__gravel_8_n.dds@c99a9592.description: Normal map of small gravel chips for di_et__gravel_c.
texture/di_et__gravel_8_n.dds@c99a9592.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/di_et__gravel_c.dds@faa32dc8.description: Fine terracotta-red and pink gravel of tiny chips with brown shadows; an even crushed-brick road surface.
texture/di_et__gravel_c.dds@faa32dc8.usage: Thundercrest and Gyrospire flats at about 20 units per repeat. Red gravel paths, house yards and road surfaces at 12 to 18 units (chips under half a unit). The red-brown matches sandstone cliffs. Pair with its normal map; seamless and even, so pair with dirt for natural variation.

texture/di_et_ext_concrete_c.dds@43f5d14.description: Clean cream whitewash render with soft clouds and fine hairline cracks; bright and smooth.
texture/di_et_ext_concrete_c.dds@43f5d14.usage: Thundercrest walls (vertical and overhanging) at about 27 units per repeat. Large whitewashed hall and shrine faces at 20 to 30 units. Measured as not seamless: use one repeat per wall panel, or hide edges at corners and trim. Bright cream may blow out in strong client light; keep for accents.

texture/di_et_ext_lgbrick_c.dds@8b2d7b81.description: Large rough-hewn tan-orange blocks in staggered courses, dark shadow grooves between them and pitted, freckled faces.
texture/di_et_ext_lgbrick_c.dds@8b2d7b81.usage: Thundercrest walls, mostly steep, about 34 units per repeat; blocks look too large there, so for village walls use 16 to 22 units (a block about 4 to 6 units wide). Orange-tan sandstone blocks that sit well with terracotta plaster. Measured as not seamless: block lines may jump at the repeat edge; hide it at corners.

texture/di_fobone_dirt_dry01.dds@2f3e076.description: Bright golden-tan dry earth with fine grit and scattered small pebbles; a clean sunlit dirt.
texture/di_fobone_dirt_dry01.dds@2f3e076.usage: Old Field of Bone ground (no measured area). Light dusty dirt for plateau, tracks and yards at 12 to 20 units; pair with its normal map (di_fobone_dirt_dry01_4n). Its sibling dry02 is the smoother, flatter version.

texture/di_fobone_sand_loose.dds@fcaf029.description: Dusty terracotta-pink sand with fine even grain and soft darker mottling; a red desert earth.
texture/di_fobone_sand_loose.dds@fcaf029.usage: Used on ground meshes of Field of Bone, Sepulcher and Arelis (about 5 units per repeat on small pieces); as terrain 16 to 24 units. The red-dust ground that matches a red-sandstone canyon: lanes, plateau dust and talus aprons below the cliffs. Seamless and low contrast, so lay gravel or paler sand patches over it.

texture/di_fp_bronze_hammered.dds@df2fcc.description: Dull tan-bronze plate with shallow hammered dents and a soft dark patina; no ornament.
texture/di_fp_bronze_hammered.dds@df2fcc.usage: Freeport City Hall walls (vertical, about 9 units per repeat). Metal door plates, roof caps, lamp housings, braziers and bronze doors at 4 to 9 units. Pair with the rust iron for fittings. Its hammered normal map is a separate asset.

texture/di_fp_ext_concrete_crumble.dds@0.description: Crumbling grey-tan render with deep pits, broken-off patches and darker stained hollows over rough stone.
texture/di_fp_ext_concrete_crumble.dds@0.usage: Freeport and Northro on walls and slopes at about 24 units per repeat. Eroded plaster, ruined wall faces and weathered grey rock at 16 to 24 units. Cold grey: place near warm textures and not beside red cliffs unless it reads as bleached stone.

texture/di_fp_ext_stonewall.dds@d7f9d67f.description: Rough rubble stone wall: orange-brown and rust blocks in irregular courses, grey-blue mortar and a little moss.
texture/di_fp_ext_stonewall.dds@d7f9d67f.usage: The commonest Freeport wall (nearly all vertical) at about 11.5 units per repeat. Village house walls, terrace retaining walls and low yard walls at 10 to 12 units; the orange stones sit well with red sandstone. A moss-free version is wanted for a dry canyon: this one keeps pale mossy patches in the mortar.

texture/di_fp_ext_street_cobble1.dds@65c.description: Angular grey-brown flagstones of many shapes with thin pale grout lines; weathered road paving.
texture/di_fp_ext_street_cobble1.dds@65c.usage: Freeport's street surface, 98 percent flat, at about 12 units per repeat. Roads, lanes and market squares at 10 to 14 units (stones 1 to 2 units). Pair with its normal map. Darker and greyer than the sandstone paving; use for the main avenue and let sandstone slabs mark special places.

texture/di_fp_ext_street_cobble1_10n.dds.description: Normal map of angular flagstone edges and grout for di_fp_ext_street_cobble1 (the @65cdd54d image).
texture/di_fp_ext_street_cobble1_10n.dds.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/di_fp_ext_stucco_lite.dds@e7ecba.description: Pale grey-pink plaster with faint green and rust flecks and a gritty, lightly stained surface.
texture/di_fp_ext_stucco_lite.dds@e7ecba.usage: Freeport East and Northro house walls at about 11 units per repeat. Whitewashed house walls and shrine plaster at 8 to 12 units. Light and slightly cool: tint warm or pair with terracotta roofs and trim, and with orange cliffs behind.

texture/di_fp_ext_tile_roof.dds@8f07b9b8.description: Rows of small rectangular terracotta roof tiles in orange, rust and brown with pale mortar lines and chipped edges.
texture/di_fp_ext_tile_roof.dds@8f07b9b8.usage: Freeport and Ro roofs on sloping and overhanging faces at about 14 units per repeat (one row under 1 unit). Terracotta house roofs and awning tops at 12 to 14 units, rows running across the slope. Warm and saturated: a natural match for orange cliffs. Pair with its normal map.

texture/di_fp_ext_tile_roof.dds@96976c1b.description: Rows of small rectangular roof tiles in a strong brick red with orange edges, pale mortar lines and chipped corners; redder and brighter than the orange di_fp_ext_tile_roof.
texture/di_fp_ext_tile_roof.dds@96976c1b.usage: Freeport West roofs (nearly all on models) at about 13 units per repeat; rows run across the slope at 12 to 14 units. The saturated red can fight a soft terracotta cliff, so use it for focal roofs and keep neighbours in the orange or brown versions. Pair with the shared roof normal map.

texture/di_fp_ext_tile_roof_7n.dds@0f41a.description: Normal map of tile rows and joints for di_fp_ext_tile_roof.
texture/di_fp_ext_tile_roof_7n.dds@0f41a.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/di_fp_ext_woodbeam_dark.dds@a16c.description: Weathered grey-olive timber with long vertical grain, a few knots and pale scuffs; sun-dried and silver at the edges.
texture/di_fp_ext_woodbeam_dark.dds@a16c.usage: The commonest Freeport and Ro beam texture (101 materials, vertical, about 12 units per repeat). Beams, posts, rafters, door frames and fences at 5 to 12 units with the grain running along the piece. This hash is not seamless (the dark2 and other hashes differ); the olive cast reads as dry old pine against warm plaster.

texture/di_fp_militia_door_common.dds@11.description: Door panel of dark vertical planks with two horizontal bands of green-patina bronze strapwork studded with diamond rivets, wood grain between.
texture/di_fp_militia_door_common.dds@11.usage: Freeport militia doors, about 7.5 units per repeat on one door leaf. One repeat per door: a village house door, gate or shutter, planks upright. The green straps stand out against warm plaster. Not for tiling over a wall. Its normal map is alpha-packed, so skip it.

texture/di_frnt_carpet_pattern_c.dds@215.description: Dark crimson carpet woven with a repeating diamond-and-leaf medallion in black-red; plush and rich but very dark.
texture/di_frnt_carpet_pattern_c.dds@215.usage: Thule house carpets (furniture archive), floor, tiling. Interior floors and long runners at 4 to 8 units per repeat. Mean value is almost black-red: use only for guild hall interiors and small rooms, never as outdoor colour.

texture/di_hp_cliff03.dds@3718fb7b.description: Horizontal bedded rock: broad pale pink-tan beds divided by a blue-grey band and thin dark lines, with a soft chalky surface.
texture/di_hp_cliff03.dds@3718fb7b.usage: High Pass Hold vertical faces at about 10 units per repeat. Calmer than cliff04: use at 18 to 26 units on a canyon wall where strata lines should read without a skyline ridge. The blue-grey band is cool, so use it in shade, not as the main sunlit colour.

texture/di_hp_cliff04.dds@764895f8.description: Layered sedimentary cliff: bands of pale salmon-pink clay, cream, slate-blue and dark grey, with a ragged battlement-like ridge along the top and wind-etched hollows.
texture/di_hp_cliff04.dds@764895f8.usage: High Pass Hold vertical faces at about 10 units per repeat (bands 1 to 2 units thick). On a canyon wall use 18 to 26 units so bands read as 3 to 4 units, horizontal. Muted pastel strata that sit between orange sandstone and grey rock; the ragged ridge fits the top of one repeat, so keep it near the rim or hide with a ledge.

texture/di_hp_cliff04_8n.dds@ae3e8267.description: Horizontal layer and ridge normal map for di_hp_cliff04.
texture/di_hp_cliff04_8n.dds@ae3e8267.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/di_kurn_wall_stucco.dds@6daf694b.description: Smooth soft-peach plaster with faint hand-trowelled swirls and a few hairline cracks; warm and clean, close to adobe render.
texture/di_kurn_wall_stucco.dds@6daf694b.usage: Old Kurn and Old Kaesora walls (mostly vertical), about 8 units per repeat. Adobe-style house walls at 6 to 10 units: the best light warm plaster for a red-sandstone village. Low contrast: use dirt and stain overlays at the base.

texture/di_kurn_wall_stucco_wornblock.dd.description: Large dressed blocks in grey-tan with peach plaster patches, dark joints and chipped corners, laid in staggered courses.
texture/di_kurn_wall_stucco_wornblock.dd.usage: Old Kaesora and Precipice of War walls (vertical) at about 11 units per repeat; blocks about 3 units wide. Ruined town wall and gate pieces at 10 to 12 units. Measured as not seamless, so keep joints off a visible repeat line by hiding it at corners.

texture/di_kurn_wall_stucco_wornplain.dd.description: Old grey-tan stucco with orange-pink patches showing through and faint green-grey mildew stains; patchy and aged.
texture/di_kurn_wall_stucco_wornplain.dd.usage: The commonest wall of Old Kurn (nearly all vertical, models only) at about 11 units per repeat. Aged house plaster at 8 to 12 units; fine beside Tak masonry or as the lower storey of village houses. The green stains suit damp places: apply with a stain overlay and not on dry clean walls.

texture/di_lolands_river_bottom.dds@d017.description: Grey-tan pebbles and shell-like fragments packed tightly, like a dry stream bed.
texture/di_lolands_river_bottom.dds@d017.usage: River and pool beds under the water line: Sunderock's river recipes apply it at the river's heights on slopes up to 45 degrees, about 13 units per repeat, with di_lolands_river_bottom_4n.

texture/di_lolands_river_bottom_4n.dds@4.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is di_lolands_river_bottom.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/di_lolands_sulfur_ground.dds@eac.description: Yellow-green sulfur crust mottled over pale ground.
texture/di_lolands_sulfur_ground.dds@eac.usage: Flats around sulfur vents: Sunderock's sulfur recipe on slopes of 8 to 45 degrees within a band of heights, about 13 units per repeat, with di_lolands_sulfur_ground_12n.

texture/di_lolands_sulfur_ground_12n.dds.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is di_lolands_sulfur_ground.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/di_morel_ext_stone.dds@89198778.description: Smooth burnt-orange stone or render with a fine brushed grain and soft darker clouds, no joints or cracks; a warm terracotta surface.
texture/di_morel_ext_stone.dds@89198778.usage: The main Morell Castle stone (hundreds of materials, mostly vertical on models) at about 17 units per repeat. Terracotta house walls, plinths and floors at 12 to 18 units: a good warm filler between pale plasters and sandstone blocks. Pair with the widely shared morel stone normal map.

texture/di_morel_ext_stone_6n.dds@0d6dc8.description: Very fine, almost flat grain normal map shared by the Morell stone textures.
texture/di_morel_ext_stone_6n.dds@0d6dc8.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat; the relief is slight.

texture/di_morel_sand_ground01.dds@8119b.description: Pale beige-grey dusty sand with soft clouds and very faint grain; the quietest and most neutral of the sands.
texture/di_morel_sand_ground01.dds@8119b.usage: Ground under Morell Castle at about 20 units per repeat, mostly flat. Good for hub town lanes, plaza edges and dust between paving; a neutral foot for walls. Avoid as the only colour near orange cliffs, where its grey reads cold.

texture/di_nest_abyss_dome2_c.dds@a5013a.description: Dark olive-brown rough rock with ochre flecks and an even grainy crumble; murky and low in contrast, a good dim cave-shell colour.
texture/di_nest_abyss_dome2_c.dds@a5013a.usage: Takish-Hiz put it on overhanging and vertical cave faces at about 12 units per repeat. For the canyon: cave-bay ceilings and the dark back walls of housing bays, shadowed rock under overhangs. Too dark and green-brown for sunlit red cliffs; avoid as an exterior wall.

texture/di_nest_abyss_floor2_c.dds@19aac.description: Plain medium-brown earth with soft cloudy darker and lighter blotches and almost no detail; a calm flat dirt tone, slightly greyed.
texture/di_nest_abyss_floor2_c.dds@19aac.usage: Takish-Hiz used it on flat and gentle ground at about 12 units per repeat. Fits cave-bay floors, worn yards in front of houses and shaded dry ground. So smooth that it can look blurred next to sharper textures: lay it under pebbles or cracks, and avoid it as the only ground on large flats.

texture/di_nest_desert_floor_8_n.dds@95d.description: Nearly flat fine-wrinkle normal map for di_nest_desert_floor_c.
texture/di_nest_desert_floor_8_n.dds@95d.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat; the relief is slight.

texture/di_nest_desert_floor_c.dds@bff50.description: Pale cream sand with a faint peach mottle and smooth even surface; the brightest warm sand in the set.
texture/di_nest_desert_floor_c.dds@bff50.usage: The Nest and Direwind flats and gentle slopes at about 11 units per repeat. Matches the floorwall strips at a cliff foot: use 12 to 20 units for plateau sand and wadi floors. Very smooth and bright: lay it under pebbles or footprints.

texture/di_nest_desert_floorwall2_c.dds@.description: A second version of the orange wall that fades into cream sand at the foot, with a more broken, patchy fringe than floorwall.
texture/di_nest_desert_floorwall2_c.dds@.usage: Same use as di_nest_desert_floorwall_c at about 12 units per repeat; alternate the two along a long cliff foot so the sand fringe does not repeat identically. Not seamless vertically; keep one repeat tall and tile only along the edge.

texture/di_nest_desert_floorwall_c.dds@3.description: The orange flowing-strata wall with a ragged edge of pale cream sand creeping up from the bottom, like drifted sand at a cliff foot.
texture/di_nest_desert_floorwall_c.dds@3.usage: The Nest's walls meeting floor, on steep and vertical faces, at about 12 units per repeat. Use as the lowest wall strip at a cliff or bay-wall base so wall rock breaks into sand: cut a band 10 to 14 units high and paint the transition, sand edge at the bottom. Measured as not seamless vertically; repeat along the edge only.

texture/di_nest_desert_wall_8_n.dds@699d.description: Fine wrinkled normal map for di_nest_desert_wall_c with soft flowing relief.
texture/di_nest_desert_wall_8_n.dds@699d.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/di_nest_desert_wall_c.dds@de11cd.description: Bright terracotta-orange sandstone streaked with flowing wavy cream and rust lines, like water-carved layers; sunlit and clean.
texture/di_nest_desert_wall_c.dds@de11cd.usage: The Nest's walls and ceilings, mostly overhanging, at about 11 units per repeat. Beautiful wall for a red canyon at 16 to 24 units with box projection; keep the flow lines running roughly horizontal. Bright and saturated, so use for sunlit faces, with darker vt_strata below. Pair with its normal map and the floorwall pieces.

texture/di_og_thatch1_roof.dds@2218cabe.description: Smeared golden-tan thatch with fine vertical streaks and soft blurred bundles; reads as straw from a distance but has no sharp detail.
texture/di_og_thatch1_roof.dds@2218cabe.usage: Ogre village roofs (Oceangreen). Distant roofs and large thatched surfaces at 8 to 14 units. Blurry up close; use the sharper well_thatch for hero roofs.

texture/di_pet_petrified_caverock.dds@f8.description: Crumbly cave rock of violet, mauve and rusty orange chips and cracks, a strongly multicolored petrified-stone look with dark seams.
texture/di_pet_petrified_caverock.dds@f8.usage: Dest and Takish-Hiz used it on steep and overhanging cave walls at about 11 units per repeat. In the canyon only as an accent inside a housing bay or a mineral vein area; the purple cast fights red sandstone if used on exterior cliffs. Pair with its normal map.

texture/di_pet_petrified_caverock_14n.dd.description: Chip and crack normal map for di_pet_petrified_caverock, with small angular relief across the whole tile.
texture/di_pet_petrified_caverock_14n.dd.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/di_rathe_walla.dds@2dcde4c5.description: Large golden-tan dressed sandstone blocks in staggered courses, pale chipped joints and rounded corners; clean and bold.
texture/di_rathe_walla.dds@2dcde4c5.usage: Rathe Chamber and Korascian walls (nearly all on models, vertical) at about 14 units per repeat; blocks 2 to 4 units wide. The best sandstone block wall for a desert city or a Tak-style ruin: city walls, gate piers, house bases at 12 to 16 units. Measured as not seamless: the course line may shift, so use box projection and break at corners. Pair with its normal map.

texture/di_rathe_walla_10n.dds@530cf7ce.description: Clear block and joint normal map for di_rathe_walla with deep joints and soft block faces.
texture/di_rathe_walla_10n.dds@530cf7ce.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/di_ro_cliff_wall.dds@dcdb41e0.description: Warm pinkish-tan sandstone with fine pitted and crumbled detail at low contrast. Reads as soft terracotta rock from a distance.
texture/di_ro_cliff_wall.dds@dcdb41e0.usage: Cliff faces. On canyonhousing's walls (canyonRock, 2026-10-20) it gave the soft terracotta of the concept art, but its fine detail streaks where it is mapped across near-vertical faces and clashes beside smooth textures such as dirtwall; pair it with textures of similar detail.

texture/di_ro_sand_grass2.dds@2cae8bf1.description: Sparse green grass tufts over tan sand, about half and half.
texture/di_ro_sand_grass2.dds@2cae8bf1.usage: Grass where sand gets water: oases, riverbanks, sheltered canyon floors. Sunderock uses it at about 13 units per repeat with di_ro_sand_grass2n; a natural step between di_tak_ruin_sand2 and full grass.

texture/di_ro_sand_grass2n.dds@a2a6548f.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is di_ro_sand_grass2.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/di_ro_sand_loose.dds@9b3f3fb0.description: Light golden-tan loose sand with faint wrinkles and a barely visible grain; clean and bright.
texture/di_ro_sand_loose.dds@9b3f3fb0.usage: Common ground texture across ten client zones, often on objects at about 25 units per repeat (flat and slope). As terrain 24 to 32 units. Brighter than sand.bmp and warmer than the pale beige sands; suits sunlit plateau dust and bleached banks.

texture/di_snarl_boulder01.dds@292efc91.description: Smooth ochre-grey rock with soft cloudy mottling and almost no cracks; the quiet sibling of di_snarl_boulder02.
texture/di_snarl_boulder01.dds@292efc91.usage: East Korlach boulders (no measured use here). Fill rock for boulders and big plain faces at 16 to 24 units. Low contrast and slightly blurred: use beside the cracked snarl_boulder02 so the detail comes from there. Its normal map is di_snarl_boulder01_8n.

texture/di_snarl_boulder02.dds@3a11979e.description: Weathered tan-ochre rock mottled with blue-grey patches, orange stains and a web of fine dark cracks; reads as old sun-baked boulder skin.
texture/di_snarl_boulder02.dds@3a11979e.usage: East Korlach terrain on overhangs and steep faces at about 32 units per repeat. A mid-tone weathered sandstone for boulders at 12 to 24 units and cliff patches at 24 to 32. Cooler grey patches suit shade and stained runs; add warmer orange beside it. Its normal map is di_snarl_boulder02_10n.

texture/di_sullon_sandpit.dds@d414fb3e.description: Khaki-brown packed sand with olive-tinted clouds and little detail, damp-looking and flat.
texture/di_sullon_sandpit.dds@d414fb3e.usage: Flat ground at Rage and Ocean of Tears at about 19 units per repeat. Fits shaded dirt yards, bay floors and river-side mud flats at 16 to 24 units. Dark and plain; avoid for sunlit dunes, and lay pebbles or tracks over it to avoid a blurry look.

texture/di_tak__ruin_grnd2_plain.dds@381.description: Brown packed earth with faint mottling; plain trodden ground.
texture/di_tak__ruin_grnd2_plain.dds@381.usage: Trails and bare ground: Goru'kar Mesa's paths recipe at about 13 units per repeat and its barren ground at about 10, with di_tak__ruin_grnd_plain_n.

texture/di_tak__ruin_grnd_plain.dds@ba0a.description: Dry packed earth in tan and brown with fine dark and pale grit flecks scattered evenly; looks like dusty trodden ground with small gravel in it. Even, low-contrast, and seamless in both directions.
texture/di_tak__ruin_grnd_plain.dds@ba0a.usage: Ocean of Tears artists laid it as a sand layer on terrain at 32 units per repeat. Good main ground for the canyon floor, plateau dust, and village lanes at 20 to 32 units; works under paving and around ruin walls. Pair with its normal map. Grit is fine, so it reads as flat colour from far away; add rock or gravel patches for variety.

texture/di_tak__ruin_grnd_plain_12n.dds@.description: Subtle fine-grain bump map for di_tak__ruin_grnd_plain, mostly flat with small pitted irregularities.
texture/di_tak__ruin_grnd_plain_12n.dds@.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/di_tak__ruin_grnd_plain_n.dds@c4.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is di_tak__ruin_grnd2_plain.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/di_tak_arch_marble_10n.dds@61846.description: Soft fibrous relief normal map for di_tak_ruin_ex_arch_marble, mostly flat.
texture/di_tak_arch_marble_10n.dds@61846.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/di_tak_int_column_trim01.dds@f46.description: Pale green-white marble pillar course: a leaf-and-bud frieze at the top, plain block courses, a rope moulding and a deep carved acanthus band below.
texture/di_tak_int_column_trim01.dds@f46.usage: Elddar columns and wall trim at an unmeasured scale (models only). Pillar bands, mantel and door-frame mouldings at 8 to 12 units per repeat, horizontal. A cool, pale accent course for Tak ruin walls; the carving reads well at distance. Keep a few of these courses on a column, not a whole wall.

texture/di_tak_int_floor_border.dds@8c82.description: Cool Tak floor border in green-grey marble: top and bottom rows of rough cobalt-blue blocks, a band of cream eight-point stars and a band of lozenges between them.
texture/di_tak_int_floor_border.dds@8c82.usage: Atiiki, Elddar and Silyssar floor edges, not seamless, about 9 units per repeat. Lay once as a strip along the edge of the pale octagon paving of the same family. The blue and teal are cold against orange sandstone; use it in a shaded temple court, not outdoors by the cliffs. The tan Takish-Hiz version of this border (di_tak_ruin_int_floor_border) is the warmer choice.

texture/di_tak_int_floor_pattern.dds@e95.description: Pale cream-grey octagon paving with diamond inlays of veined green-grey marble, outlined by fine blue-grey joint lines and set with small speckled squares between.
texture/di_tak_int_floor_pattern.dds@e95.usage: Atiiki, Silyssar, Elddar and guild-hall floors at about 13 units per repeat (models only). Clean temple or hall floor at 12 to 16 units. Much paler and cooler than the Takish-Hiz sand-coloured pattern (di_tak_ruin_int_floor_pattern), so use it indoors or in a cleaned shrine court, and let the warm one carry outdoor plazas.

texture/di_tak_ruin_ex_arch_marble.dds@f.description: Pale grey-tan weathered marble with fibrous vertical streaks and fine gold-green specks; soft and fairly even.
texture/di_tak_ruin_ex_arch_marble.dds@f.usage: Arch and column pieces of Takish-Hiz, mostly vertical, at about 13 units per repeat. Use for arches, doorway surrounds, pillars and carved lintels in the Tak ruins. Pair with its normal map.

texture/di_tak_ruin_ex_stone_crumble.dds.description: Crumbling tan stone with a fine speckled, pitted surface and dark specks; looks eroded and sandblasted rather than carved.
texture/di_tak_ruin_ex_stone_crumble.dds.usage: Used on the ruin shell models of Takish-Hiz at about 6 units per repeat, mostly on vertical and steep faces. Good for decayed ruin walls, broken pillar bases and rubble mounds at 6 to 10 units; reads as old weathered Tak stone beside the cleaner block textures. Avoid for large cliffs, where the fine grain looks like noise.

texture/di_tak_ruin_ex_tower_blockb_c.dd.description: Large weathered slabs, about three across and two high per repeat, in grey-tan stone with white fibrous mottling and dark crack-like joints between them.
texture/di_tak_ruin_ex_tower_blockb_c.dd.usage: Tower and wall faces in Takish-Hiz at about 12 units per repeat, on overhanging and steep faces. Gives big ashlar blocks 5 to 6 units wide: suits bastion bases, retaining walls and the ruined town's heavy walls. Measured as not seamless, so the joints do not line up across repeats: use one repeat per face or hide the edge behind corners and trim. Avoid tiling across wide walls.

texture/di_tak_ruin_ex_wall_block.dds@3d.description: Mottled buff-tan dressed stone with very faint block joints; the courses barely show, so it reads as a mostly even weathered wall with a hint of laid blocks.
texture/di_tak_ruin_ex_wall_block.dds@3d.usage: Exterior Tak ruin walls, mostly vertical, at about 11 units per repeat. A faint horizontal joint line runs across the middle of each repeat and shows as a seam when tiled, so use box projection and let it read as a course line. Pair with its normal map.

texture/di_tak_ruin_ex_wall_bronze.dds@3.description: Smooth burnt-ochre orange wash with soft darker and lighter clouds and a faint scratchy grain; the client names it bronze wall but it reads as clay-coloured plaster.
texture/di_tak_ruin_ex_wall_bronze.dds@3.usage: Used on the bronze panels of Takish-Hiz models at about 10 units per repeat. Good as terracotta or adobe-coloured house walls and warm accent bands against pale stone. Cloud blotches show if repeated on tall walls: keep faces under about 30 units or break with trim.

texture/di_tak_ruin_ex_wall_plain.dds@93.description: Plain mottled tan Tak stone, even and grainy with soft pale and dark clouds and no joints at all.
texture/di_tak_ruin_ex_wall_plain.dds@93.usage: Used at about 14 units per repeat on flat tops and vertical wall faces of Takish-Hiz models. Fills big wall faces, plinths and foundations between block and trim bands; also a neutral paving base. Best as the quiet partner of the block and trim textures. Avoid alone on very large faces, where the clouds repeat visibly.

texture/di_tak_ruin_ex_wall_trim02.dds@a.description: Olive-brown carved relief with two bands of interlaced scrollwork, thin plain edge strips between them.
texture/di_tak_ruin_ex_wall_trim02.dds@a.usage: Exterior wall courses in Takish-Hiz at about 8 units per repeat, on steep and vertical faces. A frieze below a parapet or around a portal. Measured as not seamless, so use one repeat vertically and do not tile it down a wall; horizontal repeat along the course is fine. Pairs with the plain Tak exterior stone.

texture/di_tak_ruin_ex_wall_trim_column..description: Fine horizontal bands of ochre stone with rows of small stars, diamonds and blocks picked out in blue-grey.
texture/di_tak_ruin_ex_wall_trim_column..usage: Column and wall courses in Takish-Hiz at about 16 units per repeat, mostly vertical faces. Gives a delicate patterned course for pillar bands and bridge walls. Fine detail disappears past about 40 units; do not use as the main wall texture.

texture/di_tak_ruin_int_column_marble.dd.description: Pale cream marble with light cloudy veining and one faint green-tinged hairline joint across the middle of the repeat.
texture/di_tak_ruin_int_column_marble.dd.usage: Interior columns in Takish-Hiz, almost all vertical, at about 10 units per repeat. Suits freestanding pillars and shrine columns; wrap round the shaft so the hairline reads as a drum joint. Avoid on large flat walls, where the single joint repeats.

texture/di_tak_ruin_int_floor_border.dds.description: Stacked border bands in grey-blue and tan: a course of small blocks, a wide diamond lattice band and a plain edge strip.
texture/di_tak_ruin_int_floor_border.dds.usage: Floor edges in Takish-Hiz, at about 9 units per repeat. Lay as a strip along the edge of the octagon paving; measured as not seamless across, so use a single strip with the bands running along the edge, not as a tiled floor.

texture/di_tak_ruin_int_floor_pattern.dd.description: Cream and gold-tan mottled paving laid as octagons with small square tiles between them, outlined by fine pale blue-grey joint lines.
texture/di_tak_ruin_int_floor_pattern.dd.usage: Flat floors in Takish-Hiz, at about 13 units per repeat. Excellent for a plaza, temple court or neutral hub paving; an octagon is about 6 units across, close to one player. Use on flat ground only and lay worn ground or sand over its edges. Pairs with int_floor_border as an edge band.

texture/di_tak_ruin_int_wall_block.dds@6.description: Pale cream-grey dressed stone with very faint block joints and light mottling; the brightest and cleanest of the Tak block walls.
texture/di_tak_ruin_int_wall_block.dds@6.usage: Interior walls in Takish-Hiz, almost all vertical, at about 8 units per repeat. For the canyon: plastered-looking house interiors, shrine and hall walls, or bleached ruin stone. A horizontal joint line crosses mid-repeat and shows when tiled. Too pale for exteriors beside red rock unless dirtied with a stain overlay.

texture/di_tak_ruin_int_wall_plain.dds@3.description: Pale grey-cream plain stone with soft grain and no joints, a notch cooler and lighter than the exterior Tak wall.
texture/di_tak_ruin_int_wall_plain.dds@3.usage: Interior walls, floors and ceilings in Takish-Hiz at about 11 units per repeat. Use for hall interiors, cave-house plastered rooms and bright stone steps. Avoid outdoors beside warm red cliffs, where it looks grey and cold.

texture/di_tak_ruin_int_wall_trim.dds@9d.description: Horizontal ornamental bands: a narrow knotwork ribbon in blue-grey and ochre above a wider band of star and lattice tiles in muted teal and gold.
texture/di_tak_ruin_int_wall_trim.dds@9d.usage: Vertical wall faces in Takish-Hiz at about 9 units per repeat, as the decorated course of an interior wall. Use as a frieze or door-surround band between plain wall textures; keep the bands horizontal. Too busy to cover a whole wall.

texture/di_tak_ruin_rock.dds@c8c2ccc3.description: Craggy olive-tan rock made of many small angular facets and chips, with brown shadow pockets and a faint yellow-green cast; reads as broken rubble rock.
texture/di_tak_ruin_rock.dds@c8c2ccc3.usage: Used on the rock models of Takish-Hiz (object use only, about 21 units per repeat). Good for boulders, rubble piles and scree-faced slopes at 12 to 18 units; a duller, greener stand-in for sandstone where the cliff should look weathered and dry. Avoid on tall cliffs at one repeat, where the facet pattern shows.

texture/di_tak_ruin_sand.dds@76f079eb.description: Soft buff-tan sand with a faint wind-smoothed wrinkle and broad darker mottling; no hard features. Reads as an even dune-colored surface at a distance and as smooth sandstone up close.
texture/di_tak_ruin_sand.dds@76f079eb.usage: Takish-Hiz used it as its main cavern shell, mostly on steep and overhanging faces, at about 31 units per repeat. For the canyon: sand plateau and river-bank flats at 24 to 32 units, or smooth buff sandstone on cave-bay walls and ceilings. Very low contrast, so break up big areas with a gravel or dirt layer and lighter sand_loose2 patches. Avoid on small props, where the blotches read as blur.

texture/di_tak_ruin_sand2.dds@a4789fca.description: Pale cream fine sand with faint soft ripples; almost featureless.
texture/di_tak_ruin_sand2.dds@a4789fca.usage: Sandy flats, canyon floors, and paths: Sunderock's ground recipes lay it on all ground at about 43 units per repeat with di_tak_ruin_sand_6n. Plain enough to need breaking up: rock_light2 on slopes, river rocks in beds, grassy sand by water.

texture/di_tak_ruin_sand_6n.dds@7f48fdc9.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is di_tak_ruin_sand2.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/di_tak_wall_block_8n.dds@ae60c2e.description: Very shallow normal map for di_tak_ruin_ex_wall_block: nearly flat with faint block-joint grooves.
texture/di_tak_wall_block_8n.dds@ae60c2e.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat; the relief is subtle.

texture/di_war_dry_riverbed.dds@845aef85.description: Sun-dried river mud in pale tan-grey, split into small plates by a dense web of deep dark cracks.
texture/di_war_dry_riverbed.dds@845aef85.usage: Devastation's dry river beds, one of the few cracked-mud textures that measured as tiling. Seasonal river bed, dried ford banks and a flood terrace at 12 to 20 units per repeat (plates 0.5 to 1.5 units). Pair with its normal map; dull in tone, so scatter pebbles over it.

texture/di_war_dry_riverbed_6n.dds@c6e44.description: Normal map of cracks and plate edges for di_war_dry_riverbed.
texture/di_war_dry_riverbed_6n.dds@c6e44.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/di_war_drygrass.dds@c9445528.description: Cracked grey-tan hardpan thickly threaded with dry straw-coloured grass blades and dark crack shadows.
texture/di_war_drygrass.dds@c9445528.usage: Devastation dry ground (no measured area). Dry scrub earth, plateau edges and the margin of dried river beds at 16 to 28 units per repeat. The grass blades make it read as grass from a distance: ideal where bare earth meets sparse vegetation. Normal map is di_war_drygrass_6n.

texture/di_war_dryground.dds@98ddb645.description: Terracotta-orange dried clay split into rounded plates by a net of fine dark cracks, with pale grit scattered on the plates.
texture/di_war_dryground.dds@98ddb645.usage: Rage's main ground, entirely flat, at about 60 units per repeat (classic scale); for a human-scale canyon use 20 to 32 units (plates 2 to 4 units). A superb dry riverbed, wadi floor or sun-baked plaza in a red canyon. Pair with the shared dryground normal map. Its olive sibling @d8cc1217 is greener.

texture/di_war_dryground.dds@d8cc1217.description: Olive-khaki dried clay in rounded plates with a net of dark cracks and pale grit; the green-grey cast of the Devastation version.
texture/di_war_dryground.dds@d8cc1217.usage: Devastation flats; use at 20 to 32 units for dry scrub earth and mud flats near water. The olive tint leaves it out of place beside the orange cliffs; mix it in small patches with the terracotta version (@98ddb645) or with dry grass.

texture/dirt_tunnel_floorwall_main.dds@5.description: Pale grey-brown earth bank with faint footprints that rises to a rough rocky lip at the top edge; a floor-to-wall piece.
texture/dirt_tunnel_floorwall_main.dds@5.usage: Freeport sewers, Mesa and Steppes tunnels, mostly on steep faces, at about 11 units per repeat. A dirt-bank-under-rock-lip for cave-bay entrances and cut banks: one repeat from floor to lip. Measured as not seamless, so do not tile it vertically; run along the edge only.

texture/dirtwall.dds@605d3ce4.description: Warm orange-tan layered rock with blocky ledges, crisp cracks, and pale weathered faces; reads as canyon sandstone.
texture/dirtwall.dds@605d3ce4.usage: Barren Coast's tower uses it at about 16 units per repeat with dirtwall_n3. A crisp warm canyon rock: cliffs at 40 to 60 units per repeat with box projection, and carved rock dwellings at closer repeats. Alternate with dirtwallb on long walls.

texture/dirtwall_n3.dds@c60e6fab.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is dirtwall.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/dirtwallb.dds@2686115b.description: A variant of dirtwall: the same warm layered orange-tan rock with its ledges and cracks in other places.
texture/dirtwallb.dds@2686115b.usage: Alternate with dirtwall to break repetition on large walls; Sunderock uses it on small forge props at about 6 units per repeat with dirtwall_n3.

texture/dreddirt.bmp@779e5a6b.description: Pale tan sun-baked hardpan with crumbling raised ridges and a cracked crust, shaded in soft browns.
texture/dreddirt.bmp@779e5a6b.usage: Dreadlands flats at about 50 units per repeat. Dry riverbed, hardpan and dusty plateau at 30 to 50 units. Measured as not seamless, so hide the repeat edges with sand or scatter; strongest as one patch between sand and rock.

texture/dredmud.bmp@72544426.description: Large polygon plates of dried grey-brown mud separated by dark, deep cracks; sharp and graphic.
texture/dredmud.bmp@72544426.usage: Dreadlands slopes at about 55 units per repeat. Dried river bed, flood plain edge and ford banks at 30 to 45 units. Measured as not seamless, so avoid wide flats of it. The Frozen Shadow copy (dredmud.bmp@51121b80) is a separate hash that measured as tiling.

texture/dsrttower_sandstone_c.dds@733c1f.description: Plain grey-tan sandstone with scratchy fine grain and soft darker clouds, the stone of the Desert of Ro towers; no joints.
texture/dsrttower_sandstone_c.dds@733c1f.usage: Used on the desert tower models of both Ro zones at about 6 units per repeat, almost all vertical. Fits plain house walls, tower shafts and low retaining walls at 6 to 10 units where block textures would be too busy. Low contrast: break with trim or plaster bands.

texture/e_tenta1_c.dds@5ffaa725.description: Market awning in vertical stripes of rust-red, teal and cream, with a drape-hem silhouette and transparent scallops cut along the bottom edge.
texture/e_tenta1_c.dds@5ffaa725.usage: Chelsith market tents, vertical, a 256 by 512 image at about 11 units tall. One repeat per curtain; alpha-tested hem; not seamless. A bolder striped canopy for the hub market at 8 to 12 units, better than the plain green and cream version for a focal stall.

texture/e_tentz_c.dds@21e2b29e.description: Market awning in vertical stripes of sage-green and cream, a drape-hem silhouette cut along the bottom edge in transparent scallops.
texture/e_tentz_c.dds@21e2b29e.usage: Chelsith market tents, vertical, a 256 by 512 image at about 11 units tall. One repeat per awning curtain, alpha-tested hem; not seamless. Market stalls and festival tents at 8 to 12 units. Stripes are soft and pale, so they read gently beside orange rock.

texture/eateryroof.bmp@69c4c223.description: Deep brick-red barrel roof tiles in rows with ribbed channels, rough pitted glaze and a few scratch marks.
texture/eateryroof.bmp@69c4c223.usage: Kaladim steep and slope roofs at about 13 units per repeat. Mission-barrel roofing at 12 to 14 units, channels running down the slope. Very dark at its mean (maroon at a distance); use on a few shaded houses or an ornate hall, not across the whole village.

texture/ew_drag_egg_desert_ext_c.dds@5d4.description: Vivid orange and cream rock with swirling flame-like streaks and dark brown pockets; very busy and stylised, like sunlit sandstone seen close up.
texture/ew_drag_egg_desert_ext_c.dds@5d4.usage: Dragon-egg desert shells in The Nest and Roost, at about 3 units per repeat. Only for small accents (a boulder, a pillar, the lip of a ledge) at 8 to 14 units; the contrast is too strong for cliff bulk. The matching normal map is a special alpha-packed image, so ignore it.

texture/ew_drag_egg_desert_int_c2.dds@88.description: Pale pink-grey and violet rock face with orange rust bands, fine cracks and chipped ledges; a colourful lit-from-the-side stone.
texture/ew_drag_egg_desert_int_c2.dds@88.usage: Inner surface of dragon-egg shells in The Nest and Roost, about 5 units per repeat. A pastel painted-rock accent for cave interiors or tall shadow faces at 10 to 18 units. Violet cast clashes with orange sandstone; use sparingly.

texture/ew_drag_egg_desert_sand_c.dds@31.description: Golden-orange packed sand with small pits, tiny pebbles and scuffed marks; a crisp lived-in desert ground.
texture/ew_drag_egg_desert_sand_c.dds@31.usage: Dragon-egg desert models in The Nest and Roost (about 3 units per repeat on small shapes). As terrain use 10 to 16 units. A detailed orange ground that suits village yards and trails; pair with its normal map.

texture/ew_drag_egg_desert_sand_n.dds@47.description: Fine pitting and grit normal map for ew_drag_egg_desert_sand_c.
texture/ew_drag_egg_desert_sand_n.dds@47.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/fg_mtentmainb_c.dds@5e978e83.description: Terracotta-orange tanned hide in big panels, fine cracked grain with lighter scuffs and darker seams.
texture/fg_mtentmainb_c.dds@5e978e83.usage: Mesa, Moors and West Wastes tent roofs (sloped, about 13 units per repeat). The most terracotta fabric in the set: tent roofs and awnings at 10 to 14 units. Pair with the khaki canvas and rust-brown dyed cloth for variety across a market.

texture/fortplanks.dds@d97b694f.description: Dark red-brown vertical planks with deep grain lines and split cracks, nailed edge to edge.
texture/fortplanks.dds@d97b694f.usage: Fort and ship walls and doors (Northro, Ro, Ocean of Tears) at about 10 units per repeat; plank width about 1 unit. Doors, gates, shutters and timber house walls at 8 to 10 units with planks upright. Rotate for floors. Dark, so pair with lighter oldwood or plaster.

texture/fortwoodcracked.dds@05b4606b.description: Warm mid-brown vertical boards with splintered cracks, knots and rough pitted ends.
texture/fortwoodcracked.dds@05b4606b.usage: Fort walls, doors and event objects across a dozen zones at about 5 units per repeat. Roughly hewn timber for house frames, shutters, fences and doors at 5 to 8 units. Pair with its normal map.

texture/fortwoodcracked_n_6.dds@42f1a240.description: Normal map of vertical cracks and board edges for fortwoodcracked.
texture/fortwoodcracked_n_6.dds@42f1a240.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/greytranswl.dds@b1eef270.description: Dark speckled grey rock above, giving way to the rose-red sandstone of cavewall2 below; repeats across, not down.
texture/greytranswl.dds@b1eef270.usage: Where dark rock meets red sandstone on a wall: map it once vertically and repeat it along the wall; the Scarlet Desert uses it at about 56 units per repeat.

texture/hp_metal_iron_rust01.dds@946449f.description: Grey-blue iron with large orange rust blooms and darker pitted patches; heavily weathered metal.
texture/hp_metal_iron_rust01.dds@946449f.usage: Metal pieces in Freeport and Corathus (about 3 units per repeat, almost all on models). Hinges, gate bars, bands, brackets, well chains and old tools at 2 to 4 units. A stronger rust than the plain iron textures; keep metal to small parts.

texture/jpsand01.dds@96871629.description: Pale cream-yellow sand with fine diagonal wind ripples and crisp grain; bright and clean.
texture/jpsand01.dds@96871629.usage: Flat ground in Nedaria's Landing at about 60 units per repeat (512 pixels, so it holds up close). Use at 30 to 50 units for sunlit sandbars at the ford, river banks and bleached dune tops. Very light: it needs sand or dirt of a darker, warmer tone beside it.

texture/justdirt.bmp@c0ea8769.description: Dark red-brown loose soil with fine pale root and grit flecks; rich and shadowy.
texture/justdirt.bmp@c0ea8769.usage: Classic zone flats at an extreme 157 units per repeat; for a village use 24 to 40 units. Damp or shaded earth in bay floors, river banks and garden beds. Too dark for sunlit plateau dust; mix with a paler dirt.

texture/katta_strata_01.dds@71813a1f.description: Pale neutral-grey stone with broad soft mottling and a few faint cracks; smooth and calm.
texture/katta_strata_01.dds@71813a1f.usage: Katta Castrum flats and slopes at about 121 units per repeat. Bleached grey stone for rims, scoured river terraces and bleached flats at 60 to 100 units. Not seamless, so use large repeats; plain, so lay strata and cracks over it. Its darker siblings katta_strata_02 to 05 are cool grey-blue.

texture/katta_strata_03.dds@1fa9f46e.description: Dark charcoal-grey stone with soft cloudy variation and a very faint rough grain.
texture/katta_strata_03.dds@1fa9f46e.usage: Katta Castrum vertical faces at about 92 units per repeat. A dark weathered grey for shaded gorges and stained cliff bands at 60 to 90 units. Not seamless; dull and cool, so only a small share beside the orange cliffs.

texture/kerrasand02.bmp@3ceec301.description: Olive-khaki dry scrubby ground with fine pale flecks like dead grass and thin dark crack lines.
texture/kerrasand02.bmp@3ceec301.usage: Flat ground of Kerra Ridge at about 60 units per repeat. A dry-scrub edge where the plateau sand meets scattered vegetation; use at 30 to 50 units. Greenish cast: use only in patches away from the red rock, and mix with sand or dirt.

texture/kl_sand_6n.dds@e2b7c70d.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is kl_sand_dirt_dead.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/kl_sand_dirt_dead.dds@8c76cb89.description: Brown dirt patched with pale dead grass.
texture/kl_sand_dirt_dead.dds@8c76cb89.usage: Dry ground with dead grass between sand and grass: Goru'kar Mesa's dry ground at about 10 units per repeat with kl_sand_6n.

texture/kl_sand_grass_dead.dds@d7162363.description: Brown-tan sandy ground sprinkled with dead olive grass blades and ochre bare patches; dry scrub with sparse growth.
texture/kl_sand_grass_dead.dds@d7162363.usage: Roost, Mesa, Devastation and the garden zone, flat, at about 15 units per repeat. Dry scrub patches at the edges of the canyon plateau, 12 to 20 units. Mostly olive-brown, so keep away from red dirt unless it is the vegetation layer. A same-looking hash (@22e5756c) is from Steppes.

texture/kl_sand_grey_dead.dds@b3065cb4.description: Grey ashy sand with paler blotches.
texture/kl_sand_grey_dead.dds@b3065cb4.usage: Grey dead ground in hollows and lairs: Goru'kar Mesa's harpy hole on slopes under 30 degrees.

texture/krakdrock.dds@9b09b1d7.description: Golden-tan sandstone slab laced with a net of fine red-brown cracks and scattered white flecks and pits; sun-baked and weathered.
texture/krakdrock.dds@9b09b1d7.usage: Plane of Fire used it on flat ground at about 32 units per repeat. A bare-rock pavement for plateau ledges, cliff-top shelves and river terraces at 20 to 32 units, sitting between sand and the cliff base. Its darker brick-red sibling krakdrock02 is much redder; do not mix them across the same face.

texture/krakdrock02.dds@8a847238.description: Dark brick-red rock, nearly even in value with faint mottling.
texture/krakdrock02.dds@8a847238.usage: Reads maroon at a distance. Too dark and saturated for soft terracotta cliffs: on canyonhousing's walls (2026-10-20) it beside pale strata bands gave candy stripes. Use for small accents, not wall bulk.

texture/kurfloor2.bmp@ed1acd41.description: Irregular crazy-paving flagstones in grey-tan and brown, many shapes, edged by dark mortar-filled joints.
texture/kurfloor2.bmp@ed1acd41.usage: Kunark floors and slopes at a large 108 units per repeat; for paving use 24 to 32 units so each stone is 2 to 4 units across. Good ruin flagstones, a river-ford crossing or a worn old road. Measured as not seamless: the polygons may jump at the repeat edge, so hide it with sand edging. A darker sibling (@e6377c42) tiles.

texture/lolands_sulfur_rock01.dds@be0d11.description: Brown rock crusted with bright orange and yellow sulfur or lichen blooms.
texture/lolands_sulfur_rock01.dds@be0d11.usage: Accent rock for sulfur springs and mineral vents (Sunderock's sulfur spires, about 37 units per repeat, with lolands_sulfur_rock01_6n); too loud for broad walls.

texture/lolands_sulfur_rock01_6n.dds@b16.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is lolands_sulfur_rock01.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/metrans03.dds@9f6190df.description: Pale speckled granite in tan, brown and grey with two thin horizontal joint lines across the 512-pixel image.
texture/metrans03.dds@9f6190df.usage: Maiden's Eye and Dawnshroud walls (all vertical) at about 20 units per repeat. Plain pale granite ashlar for retaining walls and ruin footings at 16 to 24 units; the two seams read as a block course. Peppery, so it is best at a distance with a warmer rock above.

texture/newwat1.dds@f3bc6474.description: Deep blue water flecked with white sparkles.
texture/newwat1.dds@f3bc6474.usage: A classic open-water surface (Hollowshade, Dawnshroud, the Scarlet Desert) at 26 to 116 units per repeat; too dark and blue for a turquoise canyon river.

texture/ngrass4_c.dds@00e839aa.description: Lush, dense green grass blades with a slight diagonal grain.
texture/ngrass4_c.dds@00e839aa.usage: Green meadow ground: Goru'kar Mesa's main ground at about 19 units per repeat. Too lush for a dry canyon except watered terraces and gardens.

texture/oldwindow.dds@bdebe937.description: Gold-brown cast filigree grille with leaf and oval scrollwork on a black ground, with dark rivets at the top and bottom edges.
texture/oldwindow.dds@bdebe937.usage: Akheva windows, about 26 units per repeat on vertical walls. A wrought-metal window screen, gate panel or vent grille at 8 to 14 units for one grille; the black ground is see-through only if alpha-tested, which it is not here, so it reads as a dark window behind a golden screen.

texture/oldwood256c.dds@db84cf7c.description: Weathered grey-brown boards running horizontally, with fine splits and bleached grain.
texture/oldwood256c.dds@db84cf7c.usage: Ballistae, ships and Highpass at about 3 units per repeat, mostly vertical faces. Old sun-grey timber for beams, balconies, fences, lintels and sheds at 3 to 6 units; reads as dry desert timber. Pair with its normal map.

texture/oldwood256c_6n.dds@3745b51d.description: Normal map of horizontal board grain and splits for oldwood256c.
texture/oldwood256c_6n.dds@3745b51d.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat. Measured as not seamless.

texture/rc_boulder_c.dds@0f55dd9e.description: Rust-brown granular rock speckled with pale quartz grains and chips and darker pits; a coarse red-brown stone.
texture/rc_boulder_c.dds@0f55dd9e.usage: Boulders in Dranik's Hollows (models only) at about 12 units per repeat on steep and vertical faces. Red-brown boulders and rock piles at 8 to 14 units, and a warm rocky skin for stable cliff outcrops. Dark at its mean; works as the shaded red-brown rock beside terracotta strata.

texture/redcavewal1.bmp@809cc0b9.description: Dark maroon rock streaked with black, like red granite or polished gabbro; vertical dark veins with rust-red patches between them.
texture/redcavewal1.bmp@809cc0b9.usage: Temple of Veeshan walls and ceilings at about 82 units per repeat, mostly vertical. Use 40 to 70 units for the dark volcanic back of a deep cave or a night-dark band in the canyon. Measured mean is very dark, so in client light it reads near black with red glints; keep it to accents, not whole cliffs.

texture/riverrockcvr.dds@d07da768.description: Tightly packed river cobbles of grey, tan and a few rust stones from fist to head size, dark gaps between, a little moss in the shadows.
texture/riverrockcvr.dds@d07da768.usage: Sunderock cover texture; no measured terrain use. River-bed stones for the ford and shallows at 6 to 10 units per repeat (stones then 0.6 to 1.5 units), and the stony edge of a river bank. Shows wet in the gaps, so keep it near water; blend into sand with a transition or a pebble-sand patch.

texture/riverrocks.dds@d1dea85e.description: Fine pale grey-tan river pebbles, evenly sized and tightly packed, with soft shadows between and almost no large stones.
texture/riverrocks.dds@d1dea85e.usage: Dragonscale ground texture. Pebble beaches, shallow river margins and gravel paths at 5 to 8 units per repeat (pebbles under 0.5 unit). The lightest and most even of the river stones: good where a river bank meets sand. Even sizing can look machine-made at wide repeats; mix with larger cobbles.

texture/riverrocks2.dds@7a77a868.description: Rounded river stones in browns, tans, and greys, packed shoulder to shoulder with dark gaps.
texture/riverrocks2.dds@7a77a868.usage: River beds, streambanks, stony shores, and dry washes: Goru'kar Mesa uses it below the water line at about 19 units per repeat with riverrocks_n. Reads well at the waterline beside sand.

texture/riverrocks3.dds@1bd97a4b.description: Rust-brown and red-grey cobbles of many sizes set in dark earth; warm and dirty, like a dry wash filled with sandstone rubble.
texture/riverrocks3.dds@1bd97a4b.usage: Direwind ground texture. Dry stream beds, scree aprons below red cliffs and rubble ground at 8 to 12 units per repeat. The reddish stones match sandstone and sit well between sand and a cliff foot. Dark overall; lighten with sand patches.

texture/riverrocks3.dds@9bda9fc2.description: Sandy gravel field: warm tan and orange pebbles with two big pale sand drifts spilling across them.
texture/riverrocks3.dds@9bda9fc2.usage: Sunderock. Measured as not seamless and the two drifts are conspicuous when tiled: use as a single patch at about 12 to 16 units per repeat where a sandbar covers river stones, or at a ford edge. Not for open flats.

texture/riverrocks_n.dds@97b9368b.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is riverrocks2.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/rock_canyon_c.dds@5048302a.description: Grey layered rock cut into horizontal ledges and shelves, with light weathered edges, dark gaps and rubble on each step.
texture/rock_canyon_c.dds@5048302a.usage: Brell's Rest and Pellucid, at about 24 units per repeat on flats and slopes. Stepped grey cliffs and terraced outcrops at 20 to 40 units, ledges running horizontally. Neutral grey with strong contrast: the weathered grey partner to orange sandstone. Pair with its normal map.

texture/rock_canyon_n.dds@f44dbd97.description: Ledge and rubble normal map for rock_canyon_c, with deep horizontal relief.
texture/rock_canyon_n.dds@f44dbd97.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/rock_light2.dds@d0386cbb.description: Pale tan sandstone with the same crumpled, streaked surface as rock_light5, a little lighter and less yellow.
texture/rock_light2.dds@d0386cbb.usage: Terrain slopes steeper than about 40 degrees, as Sunderock's ground recipes apply it, at about 43 units per repeat with rock_light_10n. A near twin of rock_light5, so the two alternate on long walls to hide repetition.

texture/rock_light5.dds@f972d95c.description: Ochre-yellow sandstone face with a crumpled, wind-carved surface and faint horizontal streaks; reads as warm, dry rock from a distance.
texture/rock_light5.dds@f972d95c.usage: Steep and vertical canyon walls and large rock models: Sunderock covers its cliffs with it at about 49 units per repeat. Box-project on cliffs and pair with rock_light_10n. Yellow rather than red; blends down into rock_light2 and blend_sand_rock_lg at the foot of a wall.

texture/rock_light_10n.dds@f61a9afb.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is rock_light2.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/rockcave003b.dds@b4ec786e.description: Tan-brown cracked rock with fine fissures, pale lichen flecks and small flaking plates; detailed and crisp.
texture/rockcave003b.dds@b4ec786e.usage: Rock models of Atiiki and both Ro zones at about 5 units per repeat on objects; as cliff skin 8 to 14 units. Good for boulders, rock pillars and bay walls where crisp small cracks should show; too fine for large cliffs at one repeat. A second hash of this name (grey, used on Freeport) is a different image.

texture/rockface2_c.dds@de1bae1e.description: Dark earthy brown rock, finely mottled with faint cracks and darker stains; low contrast.
texture/rockface2_c.dds@de1bae1e.usage: Goru'kar Mesa's recipes put it on slopes over 25 to 30 degrees at about 38 units per repeat with rockface_n. A dark, earthy cliff for shaded walls, cave mouths, and overhang undersides rather than sunlit red rock.

texture/rockface_n.dds@4efffe63.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is rockface2_c.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/rocksand01.bmp@07d1bc8b.description: Reddish-brown packed dirt with soft clay patches and tiny pale pebble flecks scattered evenly; a good dry trodden earth.
texture/rocksand01.bmp@07d1bc8b.usage: Flat and gently sloping ground of Cobalt Scar at about 59 units per repeat. Use 30 to 45 units for dusty canyon flats, plateau and ridge paths; the pebble flecks stay below one unit. Pair with a gravel texture for more stones and with sand for dune edges.

texture/rocksand2d.bmp@cdb258ca.description: A one-way border: dark grey-green rock with wavy lobed edges on the left, grading across to pale pebbly sandy-brown dirt on the right.
texture/rocksand2d.bmp@cdb258ca.usage: Cobalt Scar and Western Wastes used it on flat ground at about 57 units per repeat. Lay as a strip where sand or dirt meets bare rock at a cliff foot or ledge, with the rock side toward the wall; measured as not seamless across, so use it with paintTransition and repeat only along the border. The rock is cold dark grey, so best at a foot of grey or dark cave rock rather than red cliffs.

texture/rope3.dds@d14aca2d.description: Thick hemp rope in grey-brown, twisted strands running diagonally across the whole image.
texture/rope3.dds@d14aca2d.usage: Used on hundreds of EQ models and zones for rope handrails, bindings and lashings (about 4 units per repeat). On a thin cylinder or strip, map so the strands run along its length. Fine for rope bridges, awning ties and well ropes; too small a detail for any wide surface.

texture/ruin_di_tak_arch_marble.dds@3ab3.description: Cloudy cold grey stone with charcoal blotches and white speckle; weathered and stained, with none of the warm tan of the other Tak stones.
texture/ruin_di_tak_arch_marble.dds@3ab3.usage: Used on small ruin objects of Takish-Hiz. A grey weathered variant for broken arches, statue bases and cold shrine stone at 6 to 12 units; also a worn grey tone to dirty up cliff faces. Does not match the warm tan Tak walls, so keep it for contrast.

texture/ruin_di_tak_wall_bronze.dds@b46a.description: Rusty red-brown and orange oxidised plate with dark pitted blotches and pale scuffs; it reads as old corroded bronze or rough rust-coloured earth.
texture/ruin_di_tak_wall_bronze.dds@b46a.usage: Used only on small ruin objects (about 1 unit per repeat there). As a texture on doors, gates, braces and fittings at 4 to 8 units. As a dark rusty accent on a wall or rock it is a quick red-brown, but its blotches are too busy for big surfaces.

texture/ruin_tak_rug_ornate_02a_c.dds@a0.description: Faded dusty-red and pink rug in tatters, with a dark black-brown lozenge ornament across the middle and a worn, patchy weave.
texture/ruin_tak_rug_ornate_02a_c.dds@a0.usage: Takish-Hiz ruin rug, flat, about 9 units. An old threadbare floor rug for a ruined hall or abandoned house at 6 to 10 units. Unique layout; not seamless; very low contrast apart from the ornament.

texture/sand.bmp@b190cd4b.description: Warm golden-orange sand of fine even grain with faint soft dune shading and a few pale grains; the plain desert-of-Ro look.
texture/sand.bmp@b190cd4b.usage: Main desert ground of both Ro zones, Oasis and the Commonlands at about 106 units per repeat (classic terrain scale); for a human-scale canyon plateau use 40 to 60 units. Flat and gentle slopes. Low contrast, so add ripples, dirt or pebble layers; its orange sits well against red sandstone.

texture/sand3.bmp@6862adee.description: Pinkish-cream sand with broad soft dune folds and a visibly coarse, pixelated grain.
texture/sand3.bmp@6862adee.usage: Flat ground of the Timorous Deep at about 131 units per repeat. Pale pink bank sand at 60 to 90 units. The coarse dither grain shows up close, so keep it to distant plateau sand and avoid it near the player-height detail.

texture/sand3.bmp@abeffcaf.description: Tan-brown sand with soft rounded dune folds and shadowed hollows drawn across it, with fine grit throughout.
texture/sand3.bmp@abeffcaf.usage: Used on flats in Firiona Vie and the Lake of Ill Omen at about 98 units per repeat, almost all flat. Use at 50 to 70 units for plateau and bank sand where a hint of wind-shaped relief is wanted. The folds repeat visibly across a wide flat; mix with plain sand or a dirt layer.

texture/sand_loose2.dds@a342e55c.description: Pale yellow-tan loose sand, the brightest and cleanest of the plain sands: smooth, evenly lit, with only faint soft mottling and no pebbles or ripples.
texture/sand_loose2.dds@a342e55c.usage: Dune and plateau top surface, or light patches laid over a darker dirt or sand. Measured use is about 11 units per repeat on small objects; as terrain 12 to 16 units hides repetition best. Because it is so plain, add ripples or pebble scatter by other layers; avoid sheets wider than about 60 units without a second texture breaking them.

texture/sand_patch01_c.dds@a0ac9a3a.description: A ragged-edged patch of grey-brown grit, small stones and dirt on a transparent ground, about half the image clear; a stony scatter decal.
texture/sand_patch01_c.dds@a0ac9a3a.usage: Rubak flat ground, about 15 units per repeat (512 pixels). Lay as an alpha-tested decal card on flat sand to break up large areas with a stony patch at 10 to 16 units; Phase 1 has no shader blending, so the patch edge shows as a hard edge. The sand_patch02 and 03 siblings are sparser. Grey and brown tint: use over pale sand, not on red dust.

texture/sand_test_02_c.dds@04f78a87.description: Rich brown-orange packed sand and earth with soft cloudy light and dark patches and a scattering of fine specks; sharp 512-pixel detail.
texture/sand_test_02_c.dds@04f78a87.usage: Flat ground of Chelsith (reborn) at about 20 units per repeat, almost entirely flat.
