A strong base for canyon floors, trodden village ground and the dirt under houses. Warmer and darker than the pale sands: lay sand over it where wind-blown, and keep repeats between 16 and 24 units.

texture/sandstone.bmp@59a6949d.description: Dark brown flaking slabs of cracked rock with black crevices and curling edges, like peeling sandstone or sun-dried mud.
texture/sandstone.bmp@59a6949d.usage: Crushbone used it on its walls; no measured terrain use. Good for cave-bay walls, shaded undercut cliffs and the cracked bed of a dried river arm at 20 to 30 units. Strong contrast and dark crevices make it read well from far away; too dark and brown-grey for sunlit red faces, so pair with warmer rock on top.

texture/sandstone2.bmp@32de817f.description: Weathered layered sandstone in grey-brown with a mauve cast: wind-rippled ridges, dark horizontal cracks and shelf lines run across the face, so it reads clearly as bedded sedimentary rock.
texture/sandstone2.bmp@32de817f.usage: Toxxulia used it on slopes and steep faces at about 112 units per repeat; for the canyon use 70 to 110 units on big cliff faces with box projection. Cooler and duller than red sandstone, so it suits shaded walls, the lower dark band of a cliff, or cut-bank rock beside the river. Features are large: avoid on small boulders.

texture/sandstone2.bmp@f7d38e6f.description: Pale cream-grey chalky rock, bumpy and shaded in small pits and knobs, with no strata and no strong cracks.
texture/sandstone2.bmp@f7d38e6f.usage: Kerra Ridge used it on slopes and vertical faces at about 79 units per repeat. A bleached rim or high-cliff band over red sandstone at 50 to 80 units; the very light value needs a warm client light or a darker rock beneath so it does not look like snow. Avoid at tiny repeats, where the bumps turn to fine noise.

texture/sandstonebrick.bmp@596813d4.description: Olive-tan chiselled stone with chipped greenish-grey patches and shadowed hollows; despite its name it shows no regular bricks, just rough hewn stone grain.
texture/sandstonebrick.bmp@596813d4.usage: Cazic-Thule and Feerrott used it on floors and overhanging walls at about 19 units per repeat. Fits rough ruin walls, rubble foundations and tan boulder skins at 12 to 20 units. Dated classic image with a yellow-green cast, so keep it away from the sharper Tak textures and warm it with an orange rock beside it.

texture/sandstonewall3.dds@0c641507.description: Saturated golden-orange sandstone with painterly diagonal brush strokes and rounded rust-brown blotches; an amber, sunlit look with no cracks or strata.
texture/sandstonewall3.dds@0c641507.usage: Akheva used it on vertical walls and flats at about 58 units per repeat. Use as a bright sunlit gold band or a warm accent face on a red-orange canyon, not as the whole wall: the strokes and blotches repeat visibly and the colour is loud. Keep to 40 to 60 units; darken with a brown rock beside it in shade.

texture/sandtrans.bmp@1f6c162a.description: Orange sand with dune ripples and a block of cracked sandstone slabs rising out of the middle, ringed by sand drifts.
texture/sandtrans.bmp@1f6c162a.usage: Used on Commonlands slopes at a huge repeat. A stamp-like patch: one outcrop per repeat, so paint it in a spot where a rock poke-through in sand is wanted at about 30 to 40 units per repeat; do not tile across open ground or the identical outcrop repeats.

texture/sandtrans.bmp@b3ddcb13.description: Fine orange sand with a ragged patch of dark brown layered rock showing through at the upper left, with scattered stones around it.
texture/sandtrans.bmp@b3ddcb13.usage: North Ro slopes at a huge repeat. A single rock-patch stamp for sand, about 30 to 40 units per repeat; one patch per tile makes repeats obvious, so paint it sparingly beside plain sand.

texture/sarith_dirt_01_c.dds@5cb3bc8d.description: Gritty tan earth speckled with ochre, pink and grey-green chips, like decomposed rock soil on stony ground.
texture/sarith_dirt_01_c.dds@5cb3bc8d.usage: Sarith City's main ground, at about 17 units per repeat on flats and slopes. Rocky dry ground, scrub flats and path edges at 14 to 20 units; the multicolour chips break up repeats better than plain dirt. Lay under sand patches for dry scrub.

texture/sbsand01.bmp@6c6263d7.description: Golden sand drawn as soft puffy dune cells with small ripple pits and footprint-like dimples between them; stylised, painterly shapes.
texture/sbsand01.bmp@6c6263d7.usage: Stonebrunt flats and slopes at about 105 units per repeat. Works at 50 to 70 units for a classic EQ dune look on gentle slopes. The identical dune cells are easy to spot when repeated, so use it on small patches or mix with plain sand.

texture/sep_window_c.dds@81c0cd77.description: Geometric star-and-lozenge lattice in warm orange-brown wood with cream bone inlay, a central twelve-point star and a dark frame; an Arabesque screen or inlaid panel.
texture/sep_window_c.dds@81c0cd77.usage: Sepulcher fittings (overhead and vertical, about 25 units per repeat). A decorative screen, shuttered window, ceiling panel or inlaid door at 8 to 16 units, one repeat per piece so the central star stays whole. A fine accent for a desert-city hub; do not tile across walls.

texture/sgh_entry_door_01.dds@7c159e62.description: Plain door of wide warm-brown vertical planks with dark joints and light wear, edged by darker side rails.
texture/sgh_entry_door_01.dds@7c159e62.usage: Guild-hall entry doors (vertical, about 16 units per repeat). Simple house doors, barn doors and gate leaves, one repeat per leaf at 10 to 16 units. Measured as not seamless: do not tile it. Warm and quiet, so pair with a darker trim.

texture/silyssar_sandstone01_c.dds@64a42.description: Dusty rose-tan sandstone with fine even grain and soft pink-grey mottling; no joints, cracks or strata.
texture/silyssar_sandstone01_c.dds@64a42.usage: Silyssar building stone (no measured terrain use). Pink-leaning blocks, plain house walls, steps and low plinths at 12 to 20 units; a gentle pink variation to set against orange cliffs and tan paving. Soft and low-contrast: add crack or stain overlays for age. Pair with its normal map.

texture/silyssar_sandstone01_n.dds@3e533.description: Fine grain normal map for silyssar_sandstone01_c, mostly flat with small pits.
texture/silyssar_sandstone01_n.dds@3e533.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/sol_cliff05_c.dds@55101fd8.description: Honey-orange stone smooth between long wavy dark-brown flutes that run mostly vertically, like water-streaked erosion channels; no cracks and no blocks.
texture/sol_cliff05_c.dds@55101fd8.usage: Solteris and its sister zones used it on vertical and overhanging faces at an enormous 315 units per repeat. The best warm terracotta cliff candidate: use 60 to 100 units with box projection so the flutes run down the wall, and band it with a strata texture such as cavewall001b. Stylised and a little painterly; avoid tight repeats, where the flute pattern shows.

texture/sol_rock01_c.dds@72f6e7a5.description: Smooth orange-ochre rock with a faint diagonal grain and almost no detail.
texture/sol_rock01_c.dds@72f6e7a5.usage: Drew as flat orange paint when laid as thin strata ledges beside a noisy rock (canyonhousing, 2026-10-20). Fits as broad low-detail areas, not bands.

texture/somnium_dirt_03_c.dds@a4245ee5.description: Warm medium-brown packed earth with soft grain and mild lighter blotches; clean, with no stones or cracks.
texture/somnium_dirt_03_c.dds@a4245ee5.usage: Somnium slopes and steep banks at about 17 units per repeat. A quiet trodden earth for slopes, house yards and embankments at 14 to 20 units, warmer than cavefloor. Plain: add stones and cracks by other layers.

texture/sp_ft_wall_mid.dds@06a766dc.description: Courses of dark stained stone blocks with rust-red streaks and pale mortar.
texture/sp_ft_wall_mid.dds@06a766dc.usage: Built fortress walls: Wall of Slaughter's fortress at about 48 units per repeat, with di_ent_cinderblock01_mid_n.

texture/strawthatch001.dds@937a20ad.description: Pale grey-gold weathered straw thatch in overlapping layers of loose bundles; a sun-bleached cousin of well_thatch_01_c.
texture/strawthatch001.dds@937a20ad.usage: Guild hall thatch (no measured terrain use). Older weathered roofs and shelters at 10 to 16 units, running down the slope. Its normal map (strawthatch001_nrm) belongs to the Miragul copy, a different hash. Lay beside well_thatch for variation between houses.

texture/tak_bronze_detail_c.dds@bf617cee.description: Two horizontal bands of Tak interlace in gold-ochre bronze: curled spirals above and knotted beast shapes below, outlined in red-brown.
texture/tak_bronze_detail_c.dds@bf617cee.usage: Tak bronze fittings on small objects (about 1 unit per repeat there). Decorated door frames, lintel bands, altar fronts and shrine plaques at 3 to 6 units tall. Measured as not seamless: use one repeat per band. A darker brown ruin version (ruin_tak_bronze_detail_c) exists; this is the bright one.

texture/tak_rug_round_01_c.dds@c1ca46fd.description: Round woven rug: a mandala of dark red-brown lozenge medallions on a tan ground, a golden fringe all round, and transparent corners outside the circle.
texture/tak_rug_round_01_c.dds@c1ca46fd.usage: Tak rug used on a few models in Elddar, Katta Castrum and wedding chapels, flat, about 7 units wide. One rug per piece: a house floor mat or a market stall rug at 5 to 9 units, on a round disc. Needs alpha for the corners; do not tile. The ruin_ version is darker and older.

texture/tak_rug_round_03_c.dds@2fc0b8c0.description: Round carpet in crimson, black and cream: a dense floral medallion in the centre ringed by smaller flowers, with a pink-red fringe and transparent corners.
texture/tak_rug_round_03_c.dds@2fc0b8c0.usage: Rugs in High Pass Hold, Ogre villages, ships and Shard's Landing, flat, about 15 units wide. Room-sized round rug for a guild hall or a rich house interior at 8 to 15 units. Strong red: a small accent only. Alpha corners, no tiling.

texture/tak_wood_detail_c.dds@6888102f.description: Near-black olive timber carved with Tak scrollwork: spirals and tendrils above, a knotted beast panel below, across vertical planks.
texture/tak_wood_detail_c.dds@6888102f.usage: Elddar wooden fittings, small objects at about 2.6 units per repeat. Carved furniture, door panels and chest fronts at 2 to 5 units. Very dark, so the carving is visible only in strong light; usable as a detail rather than a main surface.

texture/takbs01f.dds@3e231c2b.description: Fine peach-pink sand with pale grit and rust-pink vein marks that mirror top to bottom; a warm light terracotta dust.
texture/takbs01f.dds@3e231c2b.usage: Floor and ledge ground in the Tak caves at about 13 units per repeat. A light red-sand floor for plazas, cave-bay floors and the dust at a cliff foot at 14 to 20 units. The veins reflect about the middle of the tile, so the symmetry reads on bare flats; scatter another texture over it.

texture/takbs02c.dds@94505077.description: Very dark chocolate-brown stone with a faint grain and no features; an almost plain shadowed surface.
texture/takbs02c.dds@94505077.usage: Ceiling of the Tak caves (flat-facing underside), at about 26 units per repeat. Cave-bay ceilings and the dim backs of recesses at 20 to 30 units; its darkness hides repeat. Takbs01c is near identical. Too featureless for a visible wall.

texture/takbs02wb.dds@15df9a5a.description: Deep orange-brown sandstone with fine sandy grain, faint pale veins at the top and a few darker horizontal streaks; a rich terracotta that grows darker toward the bottom.
texture/takbs02wb.dds@15df9a5a.usage: The lower walls of the Tak caves, on vertical faces at about 27 units per repeat. A darker terracotta partner for cavewall001b, or the base band of a red cliff. Not seamless vertically: use one repeat per wall section or hide the line behind a ledge.

texture/takbs02wt.dds@354e7e87.description: Dark red-brown fine-grained stone with a few soft horizontal streaks; nearly plain and very rich in colour.
texture/takbs02wt.dds@354e7e87.usage: Top of the Tak cave walls, vertical, about 19 units per repeat. A shadowed dark-terracotta wall or undercut band under overhangs and inside cave bays at 16 to 24 units. Measured as not seamless, and so plain it can look flat: add strata and cracks. Close cousin of takbs01wt.

texture/takbs06wb.dds@192dd651.description: A graded wall piece: peach-tan sandy rock at the top that darkens downward into orange-brown rock eaten by honeycomb pits and black holes.
texture/takbs06wb.dds@192dd651.usage: Tak cave wall bases on overhanging and steep faces at about 11 units per repeat. Gives an eroded, pocked foot to a cliff or the weathered lip of a bay entrance. Not seamless vertically and the top-to-bottom gradient shows: use once per wall section, not as a tiling texture.

texture/takbs07c.dds@2ed4ae17.description: Dark brown rock with lumpy relief, ochre patches and black hollows, like rough shadowed cave roof.
texture/takbs07c.dds@2ed4ae17.usage: Tak D vertical walls and ceiling, about 9 units per repeat. Ceiling and wall variety inside caves at 12 to 20 units, more textured than takbs02c. Measured as not seamless, so use patches or hide edges at corners.

texture/takbs07f.dds@2643d57a.description: Salmon-orange rock mottled with cream patches, rust spots and shallow pits; a blotchy bright terracotta with mirror-image symmetry in the pattern.
texture/takbs07f.dds@2643d57a.usage: Used on steep and vertical faces of Tak zones G and H at about 53 units per repeat. A lighter sunlit terracotta for cliff bands at 40 to 60 units; the mirrored blotches show up when repeated, so use in patches between darker bands. Too bright for deep cave interiors.

texture/takbs07wt.dds@204bba8d.description: Dark burl-like brown rock full of black pits, hollows and ochre smears; a lumpy weathered surface like honeycombed sandstone.
texture/takbs07wt.dds@204bba8d.usage: Tak G and H, about 26 units per repeat. Cave-bay walls and dark weathered ledges at 20 to 30 units, a pocked contrast to the smooth banded terracotta. Measured as not seamless: use it in patches, not across a whole wall.

texture/td_canyon_rock_c.dds@75ab4f8a.description: Near-black charcoal rock broken into angular stacked slabs with pale scuffed edges and deep cracks; hard, sharp 512-pixel detail.
texture/td_canyon_rock_c.dds@75ab4f8a.usage: Thule's Dream canyon walls, nearly all vertical, at about 51 units per repeat. A dark weathered variant for shadowed gorges, the undercut of a mesa or the cave-bay surrounds at 30 to 50 units. Very dark: it will read as black in shade, so keep to a small share of the red walls. Pair with its normal map.

texture/td_canyon_rock_n.dds@dd0e84be.description: Slab and crack normal map for td_canyon_rock_c, with strong angular relief.
texture/td_canyon_rock_n.dds@dd0e84be.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/tempredflor.bmp@20c3a1b0.description: Dark terracotta-red tiles with fine speckle, laid on the diagonal in large diamonds, divided by pale grey-tan mortar lines.
texture/tempredflor.bmp@20c3a1b0.usage: Floors of Cabilis East at about 7 units per repeat, mostly flat. Plaza paving or house floors at 7 to 10 units (a diamond is about 3 units). Measured as not seamless, so the diamond lines may break at the repeat edge: use on bounded floors rather than as open ground. Dark and heavy beside sand.

texture/thatched_roof2.dds@3fc756f5.description: Frayed grey-brown palm-leaf or reed thatch in tangled strands pointing downward; rougher and more ragged than the straw thatches.
texture/thatched_roof2.dds@3fc756f5.usage: Hut and tent roofs in both Ro zones and several others (models only, about 6 units per repeat). Rough shelters, lean-tos and the ragged edge of a thatched roof at 6 to 10 units. Drab: pair with the warm golden thatch for the main roof.

texture/thule_door_wood_c.dds@6ae6a86e.description: Carved reddish-brown wooden door sheet: scrollwork and acanthus leaves in the top left, stepped recessed panels, a brass handle slot and horizontal moulding rows below.
texture/thule_door_wood_c.dds@6ae6a86e.usage: Thule houses and Feerrott (about 11 units per repeat, 512 pixels). A unique carved entry door or cabinet front: one repeat per door at 10 to 12 units. Fits a guild hall or temple entrance. Do not tile; it is a single laid-out piece.

texture/thwall10a.dds@59456907.description: Plain golden ochre-brown plastered stone with fine speckle and soft darker clouds; no ornament, joints or cracks.
texture/thwall10a.dds@59456907.usage: Tak ceilings and overhangs at about 42 units per repeat. A calm ochre filler for house interiors, large plain walls and bay roofs at 24 to 40 units. Low contrast and slightly dull: pair with cavewall bands and trim to avoid a blank look.

texture/thwall29.dds@8bba2582.description: A framed terracotta wall panel: plain fine-grained orange sandstone between a carved floral frieze along the top edge and a matching carved band along the bottom.
texture/thwall29.dds@8bba2582.usage: The Tak walls of zone G (83 percent vertical, about 37 units per repeat). One repeat per wall bay: a temple or hall wall with carved top and bottom friezes at 24 to 36 units tall. Measured as not seamless vertically: stack one panel per bay. Warm match for the cave strata.

texture/tmtrans03a.dds@181d40d8.description: A one-way border: dark brown packed earth with fine cracks on the left, meeting a ragged lump of black-brown rough rock on the right with a clear soft edge.
texture/tmtrans03a.dds@181d40d8.usage: Kodtaz, Qvic and other Tak-side zones used the tmtrans set on flat ground at about 65 units per repeat. A dirt-to-dark-rock strip for cave floors and the foot of black cliffs, 20 to 30 units. Not seamless: use with paintTransition, no tiling across open ground. Variants 03b to 03d and 01 to 02 are neighbours with different edge shapes.

texture/twicliff01.dds@7807df97.description: Red striped cliff rock at only 64 by 64 pixels; banded but blurry.
texture/twicliff01.dds@7807df97.usage: The Scarlet Desert's giant cliff walls at about 180 units per repeat. It blurs badly at eye height; only for distant backdrop cliffs.

texture/verock2a.bmp@f36728a5.description: Dark maroon-brown rough rock with knobbly lumps, grey-lilac highlights on the ridges and black pockets.
texture/verock2a.bmp@f36728a5.usage: Veeshan walls at about 80 units per repeat, almost all vertical. Dark red rock for the deep rear of housing caves and shaded gullies at 40 to 70 units. Too dark and purple for the sunlit orange cliffs; use as the shadow end of the palette.

texture/vt_strata_01.dds@d837d156.description: Soft salmon-tan clay-rock, the lightest of the Vex Thal strata set: broad cloudy mottling, a faint rough grain and pale worn patches, no cracks or bands.
texture/vt_strata_01.dds@d837d156.usage: Vex Thal slopes and steep faces at an enormous 155 units per repeat. A soft terracotta cliff colour for sunlit canyon walls at 80 to 130 units with box projection; measured as not seamless, so the large repeat hides the edge. Reads gentle and pinkish, not candy-bright; step down to vt_strata_02, 03 and 04 for darker bands.

texture/vt_strata_02.dds@70fb0f70.description: Mid terracotta clay-rock with fine rough grain and soft darker pockets; a warm red-brown with low contrast.
texture/vt_strata_02.dds@70fb0f70.usage: Vex Thal steep and vertical faces at about 130 units per repeat. The main soft-terracotta wall colour for a red canyon at 80 to 130 units; measured as not seamless, so avoid tight repeats and tile it over big faces only. Mixes with strata_01 above and strata_03 below.

texture/vt_strata_03.dds@e077e15c.description: Chocolate-brown clay-rock with fine rough grain and a slightly rusty cast; the middle-dark step of the Vex Thal set.
texture/vt_strata_03.dds@e077e15c.usage: Vex Thal steep faces at about 145 units per repeat. Darker lower or shaded band under the terracotta strata_02, or the colour for cave-bay surrounds at 80 to 130 units. Not seamless; keep repeats large and break edges with a ledge.

texture/vt_strata_04.dds@3f671c4f.description: Dark roasted-brown rock with pitted rough grain and darker lumpy hollows; a shadowy near-black brown.
texture/vt_strata_04.dds@3f671c4f.usage: Vex Thal vertical faces at about 136 units per repeat. Cave-bay interiors, undercuts and the dark base of a cliff at 70 to 120 units. Not seamless; sunlight turns it chocolate, shade turns it black.

texture/vt_strata_05.dds@2029fcd6.description: The darkest and roughest of the Vex Thal strata: near-black brown rock with lumpy pitted relief and faint reddish highlights.
texture/vt_strata_05.dds@2029fcd6.usage: Vex Thal flats and slopes at about 27 units per repeat; the only one of the set measured as tiling. Cave floors, ceilings and deep shadow rock at 24 to 40 units. Too dark for any sunlit face.

texture/vtwall14.dds@427fe5dc.description: Dusty terracotta clay render with hand-smoothed wavy ridges, trowel marks and small cracks; a warm adobe wall.
texture/vtwall14.dds@427fe5dc.usage: Vex Thal walls (vertical and overhanging) at about 28 units per repeat. The best true adobe wall: house walls, kiln-like huts and village retaining walls at 16 to 28 units. Tiles cleanly; mid-value and warm, so it sits next to terracotta cliffs without clashing. Add dirt at the base.

texture/wartents_orc01_10_n.dds@f3ceba01.description: Normal map of stitched panel seams for wartents_orc01_c.
texture/wartents_orc01_10_n.dds@f3ceba01.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/wartents_orc01_c.dds@df432ecd.description: Patchwork tent hide: irregular orange and olive-brown polygon panels joined by rows of pale stitching.
texture/wartents_orc01_c.dds@df432ecd.usage: Orc tents of Commonlands, Ro, Freeport and Toxxulia at about 24 units per repeat on tent roofs. Tent canopies and awnings at 16 to 24 units. Panels and stitching read strongly: use on a few big pieces, not many small ones. Pair with its normal map.

texture/wartents_orc02_c.dds@af1fb7b6.description: Fuzzy tan hide divided into large panels by thin dark stitched seams.
texture/wartents_orc02_c.dds@af1fb7b6.usage: Orc tent walls in many zones at about 10 units per repeat. Tent walls, door flaps and stall covers at 8 to 12 units. Calmer than orc01; the seams give a hand-sewn look without the loud patchwork.

texture/wartents_orc03_c.dds@262f6313.description: Soft blurred tan-pink hide or canvas with cloudy mottling and no seams or stitching.
texture/wartents_orc03_c.dds@262f6313.usage: Orc tents (many zones, Barren, Ro, Mesa) at about 15 units per repeat. Plain canvas awnings and tent covers at 10 to 16 units. Blurry up close: use at distance or under other detail.

texture/well_thatch_01_c.dds@61eac4f1.description: Golden-straw thatch hung in overlapping rows of loose bundles with dark shadow between layers; warm and tidy.
texture/well_thatch_01_c.dds@61eac4f1.usage: Thatch of huts, wells and furniture across ten client zones, at about 16 units per repeat on sloping and overhanging faces. Roofs of huts, awnings and shade shelters at 10 to 16 units, straw running down the slope. Pair with its normal map. Cleaner and warmer than the grey strawthatch001.

texture/well_thatch_01_n.dds@a113aa82.description: Strong straw-bundle normal map for well_thatch_01_c, with long vertical strands and layered ledges.
texture/well_thatch_01_n.dds@a113aa82.usage: Use only with its diffuse at the same repeat.

texture/wtr_waterfall_tileb.dds@c3790289.description: Frothing white water with pale teal under the foam, streaked top to bottom, edges fraying into transparency.
texture/wtr_waterfall_tileb.dds@c3790289.usage: Heavy white falls, cascades, and geysers (Sunderock's geyser, about 130 units per repeat); the base of a fall that uses wtr_waterfall_tilec above.

texture/wtr_waterfall_tilec.dds@970059de.description: Falling water: teal sheets streaked with white foam running top to bottom, its side edges fraying into transparency.
texture/wtr_waterfall_tilec.dds@970059de.usage: Waterfall faces: map it so the streaks fall down the face; Sunderock's waterfall models stretch it about 190 units per repeat. The frayed alpha suits falling water, not pools; pair with wtr_waterfall_tileb where the fall whitens.
